zh.place: 布鲁克林 Adrian的旧公寓

zh: 七点十二分，布鲁克林的天还是一层脏灰。暖气片咣当响了两声，吐出一股铁锈味的热气，窗玻璃上糊着一层白雾。
廉价咖啡机又卡住了，红灯一闪一闪。洗衣机甩干时一下下撞着墙，震得台面上的马克杯一点点往边上挪。
水龙头关不严，一滴，一滴，砸在昨晚的外卖盒上。盒盖翘着，冷掉的炒面结成一坨，酱汁凝成一层褐色的膜。
他六点一刻就醒了。楼梯间里拖鞋一路啪嗒啪嗒响下去——3B的Ortiz太太下楼拿报纸，三年来没早过、也没晚过一分钟。
门把手上挂着一袋垃圾。上礼拜楼管Hector拿自行车链条把后门从里面锁死了，说是防流浪汉。现在倒个垃圾，得从前门绕半个街区。
手机屏幕亮起，冷白的光照着两条通知：活期账户 $32.18。房租周五到期。
Adrian一米八二，赤脚踩在冰凉的地砖上。灰色旧T恤领口洗得发松，却被一副宽肩撑得紧绷，后背绷出肩胛骨的形状。
下颌一层青黑的胡茬，两天没空刮。运动裤松松挂在胯骨上，手腕上那块二手电子表的塑料表带裂了，用黑胶布缠着。
他抬起一只大手，掌根照着咖啡机侧面“砰”地一拍，手背上的青筋一根根绷起来。机器呛了一声，终于开始往下滴。
手机夹在肩膀和下巴之间，胡茬蹭着屏幕沙沙地响。老板的声音从听筒里挤出来：客户改方向了，全部重来。
全部重来。说得真轻巧——我连重煮一壶咖啡都得先算算电费。
那天早上，我账户里只有32美元。
十年前。夜雨把便利店门口的霓虹泡成一摊摊晃动的红和绿，雨水顺着塑料遮阳棚往下淌，空气里是湿柏油和关东煮的味道。
十七岁的Adrian蹲在台阶上，外套湿透贴着背，指关节也破了——刚才那一架是两个人一起打的。他用牙撕开创可贴，按上十八岁Roman裂开的嘴角。
Roman的指节全是新鲜的擦伤，血混着雨水往下淌。他一声没吭，只盯着Adrian的手指，呼吸很重，带着薄荷糖和铁锈的味道。
两人同时抬眼，近得过分。Roman的拇指碰了一下他耳后，指腹粗糙、滚烫。雨声一下子变得很远。差半寸。
没亲上。差半寸。第二天我跟自己说，是雨太大，是他挨了一拳脑子不清楚。这话我说了十年，耳后那块皮肤一次都没信过。
第二天早上，他就没了。Adrian发了三条消息，第四条打到一半，删了。从那以后，他宁可绕两条街，也不再从那家便利店门口过。
关于父亲，母亲留下的永远只有一句：很复杂。说这话时，她总在擦一只早就干净了的盘子。
Adrian把那句“很复杂”和十年的空白一起咽下去，挤进早高峰的地铁。车厢里是湿羽绒服、廉价香水和别人的咖啡味。
我以为我的人生大概就这样了：改稿，交房租，夹在别人的胳膊肘中间，一路站到终点。
一声急刹，轮胎在湿柏油上尖叫。三辆黑色SUV齐齐停在旧公寓楼下，车身亮得能照出整条街的破败。

zh.hint: 楼下三辆车刚停稳，你的手机就响了。未知号码。
lines: roman
……Adrian。
roman
别挂。往窗外看。
roman
第二辆车。我在下面等你。
roman
八点零五。我不上楼——你下来。
then: 电话断了。十年没人这么叫过他的名字，可那个声音，他只用了半秒就认了出来。
skip: Adrian按掉了未知来电。三秒后，楼下，第二辆车的门开了。

zh: Roman从第二辆车后走出来。黑西装，耳后一枚通讯器，雨后的风掀不动他一根头发。十年没见。

zh.t: THE HEIR HE CAME BACK FOR

zh.place: 布鲁克林 公寓楼下

zh: 老板最后一条消息还停在屏幕上：中午前改完。Adrian用肩膀撞开那扇总卡住的玻璃门，门轴干涩地呻吟了一声。
他套了件洗旧的军绿夹克，牛仔裤膝盖磨得发白，脚上一双开了胶的工装靴，鞋带随手一系。
帆布包斜挎在宽肩上，里面那台旧笔记本的风扇还在嗡嗡转。他一手攥着凉掉的咖啡，一手拎着那袋垃圾，指节上沾着昨晚的马克笔印。
先是声音。三台大排量引擎压着同一个低频怠速，脚下的井盖跟着嗡嗡发颤，震得他鞋底发麻。
然后才是车。三辆黑色SUV首尾相接，堵死了半条街。车窗黑到底，车漆亮得像刚从水里捞出来，照出整条街：锈掉的消防梯，歪倒的垃圾桶，还有他自己。
平时停满外卖电动车的路边，清得干干净净。对街熟食店的老板拎着拖把愣在门口，连鸽子都退到了屋檐上。
第一个念头：我到底欠了谁的钱，能欠出三辆这种车来。
他把垃圾袋慢慢放在台阶上，空出右手。在这种街上长大的人都有这个习惯：先空出一只手。
第二辆车门打开。Roman看人之前先扫一圈四周——屋顶、窗口、街角。紧张时下颌收紧。这些，Adrian全认得。
认得太快，这才让人恼火。脑子还要一秒，身体一秒都不用——胃里先往下一沉，手里的纸杯被捏瘪了一角，凉咖啡顺着指缝往下淌。
Roman直起身，一米八八的个子把车门框都衬矮了。黑西装剪裁贴身，没系领带，白衬衫领口敞着一颗扣子。
十八岁的Roman肩背还没长开，瘦得像根没打磨的木头。现在黑西装是被肩线撑出形状的，胸膛宽得能挡住半扇车门。
皮鞋锃亮，踩过积水不溅一滴。左腕一块钢表，表盘素净，表带却压不住底下那道发白的旧疤。
头发剃得很短，贴着头皮一层深色的茬。下颌线利得像刀削，压着一层青色胡茬。左耳后，通讯器的细线没进领口。
然后是那双眼睛。灰色的，像冬天河面上的薄冰。落在Adrian脸上的那一刻，冰面裂开一道缝。
风掀起他领口一角：锁骨下一道旧疤，颜色比皮肤浅，像一截被缝上的闪电。
这十年你死哪儿去了？——不对，先问锁骨下那道疤是谁干的。不管是谁，我去宰了他。
Adrian有十年的问题要问，视线却先往下走，在那截锁骨上多停了一秒。喉结滚了一下。

zh.hint: 他抓到你在看他。十年没见，第一回合就落了下风。

opts.t: 完全没有。
then: Roman的眼神在他脸上停了半秒，喉结上下滚了一下。随即又冷成一块铁，像什么都没发生。
opts.rthink: 完全没有。他十七岁撒谎也是这腔调，尾音往下压。三年隔着长焦看他，今天头一回被他看回来。

opts.t: Adrian别开脸，下颌一绷，假装对那串车牌号产生了浓厚兴趣。
then: Roman没拆穿。嘴角很短地动了一下，快得像风刮过刀口。
opts.rthink: 那串车牌是假的，我昨晚亲手换的。他盯得这么认真，耳根却红到了领口。

opts.t: 你先说。你看够了吗？
then: 话一出口，他自己的下颌先绷紧了，太阳穴边一根青筋轻轻跳了一下。
opts.rthink: 没够，十年都没够。评估风险——这条街上最大的风险，正扬着下巴站在我面前。

zh.hint: 他还在看你，下巴扬着，跟十七岁时一样不服输。十年了，你还是不知道该先说哪句。

opts.t: 上车。
我知道你有很多问题。先上车。
then: 话说得很稳，搭在车门上的那只手却收紧了，指节泛白，手背上青筋一根根浮起来。

opts.t: Roman伸手想碰他手臂，指尖离夹克只差一寸，停住，又收回。“上车，Adrian。”
then: 那只停在半空、微微发颤的手，Adrian看见了。

zh: Adrian走到他面前，靴底碾过一滩积水。他比Roman矮不了多少，下巴抬着，胡茬底下的咬肌绷成一道硬棱。
近到能闻见他身上的味道：雪松、枪油，还有一点冷掉的烟。十年前，他身上只有薄荷糖。
他没再争，自己拉开后座车门，一只手撑在门框上方。那姿势像在替人挡刀，也像在堵死退路。

zh.hint: 这句话你在车里练了四十分钟，掌心都练出了汗。没有一种说法是对的。

opts.t: 你父亲昨天去世了。
Adrian，先听我说完。……你父亲昨天去世了。
then: 他说得很慢，一个字一个字，灰眼睛一直没离开Adrian的脸，像在等一拳挥过来。

opts.t: Roman没开口，把平板递过去。讣告停在屏幕上。
then: 黑底白字，冷得像墓碑。Adrian看清了标题：ALEXANDER VALE，昨日辞世。

zh: Adrian脸上的讽刺第一次消失了。像有人一把扯掉了他一直举在身前的那块盾。
街上的声音全退远了。他只听见自己的心跳，一下，一下，沉得像有人在楼上拖一只铁箱子。

zh.title: 你父亲是Alexander Vale
zh.txt: 酒店、银行、航空、媒体——曼哈顿天际线上一半的名字。就是那个Vale。

zh: 车门合上，“咔哒”一声，像保险柜落了锁。旧公寓、便利店、公交站牌，被深色隔音玻璃一点点甩到身后。
车厢里是新皮革和冷气的味道，安静得能听见出风口的细响。他那条磨白的牛仔裤搁在奶油色真皮上，像个闯进来的贼。
Roman坐在他旁边，西装裤绷在结实的大腿上，膝盖离他只有一拳。车一转弯，那点体温就隔着布料晃过来。
Roman从前排接过一只黑色皮面文件夹，放到Adrian腿上。手离开时，在他膝头多停了不到一秒。
黑色小牛皮文件夹，比他那台旧笔记本还沉。封面没有字，只在右下角压着一个烫银的V，边角磨得发亮——这东西有人翻过很多遍。
里面的纸厚实，对着窗光能看见暗纹。第一页：ALEXANDER VALE，已故。第二页：亲子关系确认。第三页：ADRIAN HALE，匹配度99.998%。
他没翻资产页，先把DNA结果来回看了两遍。拇指压在那串数字上，指甲盖都压白了。
这个数字精确到没法拿“弄错了”安慰自己。
没有雷声，没有配乐。他的人生，就在一辆安静得过分的车里，被一张昂贵的纸改写了。
二十七年，我连他一张照片都没见过。现在他死了，倒想起来往我腿上塞一份亲子鉴定。
他昨天刚死。所以今天我突然成他儿子了？
Roman给了他几秒，看着他的喉结上下滚了两回，才划开平板：VALE集团——控股受益继承人。
屏幕最上方是一张卡片。哑光黑底，压着一道极细的金边，正中一个数字框，盖着一层磨砂似的封印。他只看得出，那串数字很长。
卡片下面是一列标志，一个接一个：他每天坐地铁路过的那家银行，公司楼下他从没进过的那家酒店，机场跑道尽头那排印着V的白色机尾。
他发现自己的拇指已经搭在那层封印上了。他把手收回来，在牛仔裤上蹭了一下。
替人写了五年广告，“改变人生”这四个字我写过不下一百遍。原来它真来的时候长这样：一个打不开的框。
多到具体数字已经没什么帮助。控股权、私人航空、酒店、媒体、地产、银行。
我今天早上，账户里还剩32块18。
存你那32块的那家银行，现在有你的股份。

zh.hint: 那串还没看清的数字就摊在你腿上，沉得像一块烧红的铁。你的第一反应是——

opts.t: 把完整资产清单给我。别给摘要。
then: Adrian一把把平板转回来，指腹在屏幕上划得飞快。
我只是比较喜欢拿着资料震惊。
Roman嘴角很轻地动了一下，像冰面底下有鱼游过。屏幕上依次展开：黑卡、曼哈顿顶层、私人航空、董事会临时投票权。
opts.rthink: 他要清单，不要摘要。好。只要他别问是谁整理的——那份清单，我三年前就背熟了。

opts.t: 我母亲知道吗？
then: Roman的表情第一次真正变得谨慎，下颌那块肌肉动了动，像在嚼碎一句不能说的话。
这是我现在能给你的答案。
Adrian的手指压住那页资产，指节一根根凸起，纸面被按出一道折痕。
你母亲做过一些选择，就是为了让你远离这个家族。

then.title: 线索：母亲知道得更多
then.txt: 那笔钱有整整三秒不再像奖励——更像一扇母亲替你死死抵了二十七年的门。

opts.rthink: 她知道的，比我能说的多。他再往下问一句，我就得在撒谎和让他恨她之间选一个。

opts.t: Adrian拇指一按，直接把资产页按灭。
then: 我更想知道，为什么偏偏是你来告诉我。你知道多久了？
Roman停了一下。窗外的光一格一格扫过他的脸，照不进那双灰眼睛。
三年。这两个字比那串数字砸得更狠。钱能解释那些车，解释不了他看了三年，却一次都没走近。
opts.rthink: 四十八亿，他一拇指按灭了。他从来不先看钱，先看人。我倒宁可他先看钱。

opts.t: 停车。我要自己确认。
then: 今早6点14分，有人侵入了你住处的监控。
他把自己的加密手机推过来，黑色机身上还带着他掌心的温度。
DNA你可以查，我可以查，律师也可以查。但不能停在这儿查。
实验室回执、Vale官方讣告、Roman的安保授权、律所登记。Adrian一个个查过去，拇指越划越慢。全是真的。
opts.rthink: 停车？6点14分以后，这条街每扇窗我都没把握。他真要下车，我就把人扛回来，再挨他一拳。

zh: Roman在平板右上角轻点一下，食指上一层薄茧。那页资产缩了下去，换成四格黑白监控，雪花点沙沙地跳。
继承说明书里不会写的那部分。你楼里的监控，今早6点14分被人动过。这是那一分钟的四个画面。
大概率。另一种可能更糟。
车里的冷气像忽然又低了两度，Adrian后颈的汗毛一根根立起来。
这是第一次，这笔继承不再只是荒唐，而是危险。
四格画面，同一个时间码：06:14。Adrian一格一格看过去。
CAM A，楼梯间：一个裹着睡袍的老太太扶着栏杆往下走。3B的Ortiz太太，下楼拿报纸。
CAM B，前门台阶：外卖员把两袋东西往台阶上一放，冲着镜头打了个巨大的哈欠，转身就走。
CAM C，后门：一个穿工装夹克、拎工具箱的男人从巷子里过来，像来修暖气的。他握住门把一拉，门开了，他侧身进了楼。
CAM D，门厅：楼管Hector拎着拖把桶，一下一下拖着地。
乍一看什么都没有。一栋破楼，一个早上，四个再普通不过的人。

zh.hint: Roman把平板转过来：“你在那栋楼住了三年。哪里不对，你比我清楚。”
zh.title: 监控画面 · 6:14
zh.hint2: 线索：Ortiz太太每天6:15下楼拿报纸；楼管Hector上礼拜用自行车链条把后门从里面锁死了。四个画面里，有一件事不可能发生——点它。

cams.clue: 6:15前后，Ortiz太太下楼拿报纸——三年来天天如此。
外卖员正脸对着镜头打哈欠，放下袋子就走。
后门上礼拜就被Hector从里面锁了链子。这人却从外面一拉就开——全程背对镜头，每一步都踩在死角上。
楼管Hector在门厅拖地，一切照旧。

win: 后门。上礼拜Hector从里面上了链子，从外面根本拉不开。
Roman侧过脸看了他一眼。那一眼很深，像在确认一件早就知道的事。
他知道。他凭什么知道我们楼后门上了链子？

win.title: 线索卡：内部知情
win.txt: 上了链子的门，他一拉就开；摄像头的死角，他一个不落——对方熟悉Vale的安保系统。

后门上礼拜就从里面锁了链子，从外面拉不开。他一拉就开了。
……他怎么知道我们楼后门上了链子？

t: roman
后门那个死角，三年前我就报过修。没人修。今天有人用上了。不管他是谁，敢碰Adrian一根头发，我就亲手教他什么叫死角。

zh.place: Vale车队 · 去机场的路上

zh: 黑色SUV的车窗贴着深色膜，九月的晨光透进来，只剩一层冷淡的灰蓝。车里是新皮革和雪松香氛的味道，干净得不像有人坐过。
Adrian坐在后座靠窗那侧，一米八二的个子窝在宽大的座椅里也舒展不开。军绿夹克洗得发旧，里面那件灰T恤领口松垮，工装靴鞋头开了胶。
他一夜没合眼，下颌冒出一层青黑的胡茬，眼下挂着阴影。一只大手搭在膝盖上，指节还因为攥了太久而泛白。
Roman坐在他旁边，背挺得笔直。黑色西装剪裁贴身，肩线又宽又硬，白衬衫的领尖一丝不乱，左耳一枚透明耳麦，细线没进衣领。
深色的头发剃得很短，贴着头皮一层。灰眼睛盯着前路，像在默数每一辆擦过去的车。腕上一块钢表，表带下压着一道浅白的旧疤。
十年没见，他坐着都像一把收进鞘里的刀。我呢，T恤领口洗松了，胡子两天没刮，靴子还张着嘴。

then: 三年。这个数字像一枚钉子，从布鲁克林那栋红砖楼一路跟着他，跟上了被晨雾打湿的高速。
Roman的侧脸映在深色车窗上，一动不动，连下颌那条线都没松过。
else: 杯架里那杯是你的。两份糖。
Adrian低头。咖啡还烫，两份糖，没加奶。这事他一个字都没提过。如果Roman今天才接的活，凭什么连这个都知道？

else.hint: Adrian问到了。他的眼睛钉在你脸上，下颌绷着，车里只剩轮胎碾过路面的沙沙声。你可以撒谎，可以拖，也可以说实话。

opts.t: （沉默半秒）三年。
……够久了。
Roman没回答，指腹在平板上一划，屏幕的冷光照亮他的指节：任务起始日期，三年前的今天。
then: Adrian盯着那个日期，喉结滚了一下，很久没出声。

zh: 三年。意味着Roman知道他从皇后区搬进布鲁克林那间漏雨的阁楼，知道他换过三份工作，知道他周末给搬家公司打零工，扛着冰箱爬五楼凑房租。
知道去年冬天，他在酒吧后巷被两个人堵住，挨了一拳，还了三拳，回家对着浴室镜子，自己给手背缝了六针。
知道他打野球崴了脚踝，硬撑着打完最后一局，一瘸一拐走了二十个街区回家，第二天照样去上班。
被一个人扔下其实很简单：恨他，然后慢慢忘掉。可现在才知道，他一直就隔着一条街、一扇车窗看着——这比被扔下更难咽。
后巷那晚，我一个对两个，针线是在楼下杂货店买的。他要是就在街对面看着——那最好也看清楚了：我没喊过一声救命。
街对面。我刚要过马路，你已经用不着我了。
你的右勾拳，比十七岁的时候沉。
Adrian下颌一紧。被他夸这一句，比挨的那一拳还让人火大。

zh.hint: 三年，他就站在街对面，看你扛货、挨揍、还手，一次都没过马路。你怎么处理？

opts.t: 行。我先信你一半。
then: Roman看了他很久。灰色的眼睛里有什么东西沉下去，又慢慢浮上来。
opts.rthink: 一半。十年前他把全部都递给过我，我没接住。剩下那一半，我拿命去换也认。

opts.t: 西装穿得再好看，跟踪也改不了名叫保护。
then: Roman低头扫了一眼自己笔挺的前襟，又抬起眼，一侧眉峰挑起一点。
opts.rthink: 他说我西装好看，前半句我收了。后半句他说得对——后巷那晚，我自己也这么骂过自己。

opts.t: 是我父亲雇的你？
then: Roman的瞳孔缩了一下，下颌的肌肉跟着一跳。很快，但Adrian抓到了。

then.title: 线索：父亲可能雇了Roman
then.txt: Alexander Vale，在死前三年就找到了他——比任何一份遗嘱都早。

opts.rthink: 老Vale三年前找到我，只提了一个条件：别让他知道是谁雇的。我刚用半个眼神违了约。

opts.t: 所以我周五晚上在哪儿喝酒、喝到几点，也都写进报告了？
then: Roman转头看向窗外，喉结在硬挺的领口上方滑了一下。
第七大道那家。吧台左数第三个位子，一般喝到一点四十。
Adrian笑出了声。低沉，带点熬夜后的沙哑，胸腔都跟着震。
那个酒保给你免过三次单。账目异常，我得记。
可他搭在膝上的手已经攥成了拳，手背上的青筋一根根浮起来，下颌绷得像要咬碎什么。
账目异常。一个酒保请我的三杯啤酒，他记成了账目异常。行，记下了——这人也有绷不住的地方。
opts.rthink: 第三次免单那晚，那酒保的手搭上了他的肩。那份报告我改了四遍，最后只剩‘账目异常’。

zh: 窗外的红砖楼和投币洗衣店一点点退远，换成机场外围灰扑扑的辅路、铁丝网，和一排排没有表情的货运仓库。
十年前，Roman就在他身边；然后整整七年，音讯全无；三年前，他又以“保护”的名义回来，却始终没露过面。
中间那七年，像被人拿刀从时间轴上齐齐剪掉，断口干净，连一根线头都没留。
Roman搭在膝盖上的手指慢慢收紧，指节一根根顶起来，把西裤的布料攥出几道褶。
Roman终于转过头。那双灰眼睛直直看过来，近得能看清里面压着的东西。
十年前的夏夜，雨下得又闷又密。便利店门口的空调外机嗡嗡震着，荧光灯管在头顶滋滋作响，积水里映着一片惨白。
十八岁的Roman靠着冰柜坐在地上，嘴角裂开一道口子，血已经干成暗红。指关节擦破了皮，T恤领口被人扯歪了。
Adrian用牙撕开创可贴，手不太稳。贴上去的时候，两个人越靠越近，近到能闻见他身上雨水、铁锈和薄荷糖混在一起的味道。
Roman的拇指擦过Adrian耳后，粗糙，滚烫。两个人的嘴唇之间，只差半寸。
外机还在嗡嗡地响。雨砸在雨棚上。谁都没有动。
再一眨眼，眼前是二十八岁的Roman，不到一臂远。肩膀比当年宽出一圈，那副骨架把西装撑得严丝合缝。
他的嗓音低得发沉。衬衫领口随着呼吸一起一伏，硬挺的领尖底下，隐约露出锁骨下一道旧疤的末端。
十七岁时，想亲他是件让人困惑的事。二十七岁，麻烦在于他太清楚自己想要什么——想要到牙根发酸。
冷静。他是你的保镖。你付他工资——行吧，是你那个死掉的爹付。

zh.hint: 那半寸悬在你们之间，悬了整整十年。车厢里只剩空调低低的风声。这一次，你动不动？

opts.t: Adrian伸手，粗粝的指腹碰上他腕上那道浅白旧疤。
then: Roman本能地扣住他的手腕。快得像拔枪，力道却轻，拇指正好压在他突突直跳的脉搏上。
掌心的热度在他腕骨上多停了半秒，才松开。
opts.rthink: 腕上这道不算什么。疼的在锁骨下，是走的那年换来的。他再问一句，我差点就全说了。

opts.t: 车身转弯，Adrian的膝盖顺势贴上他的大腿，没有移开。
then: 隔着薄薄的西裤，Roman腿上的肌肉绷成一块铁。他垂眼看了一下，睫毛压得很低。
Roman往后靠进座椅里，像要拉开距离。膝盖却一寸都没挪。
这已经算回答了。Adrian转头看窗外，没让自己笑出来。
opts.rthink: 该挪开。腿上每块肌肉都在等命令，我一条都没下。这一路还剩几个弯，我开始数了。

opts.t: Adrian什么都没说，只是盯着他的嘴。
then: Roman说话慢了下来，喉结在硬挺的领口上方重重滚了一下。
你什么都没做的时候，通常最危险。
opts.rthink: 他盯我的嘴，跟便利店那晚一模一样。那晚我停了，第二天就走了。他到现在都以为这是两件事。

opts.t: 以后再说。先处理继承。
then: 也许十年终于教会我边界。
Roman很轻地笑了一下，鼻腔里短促的一声。
opts.rthink: 他停了，我该松口气。可那个十七岁从不踩刹车的人，是我亲手教会他刹车的。

zh.place: 泰特伯勒 私人机库

zh.title: VALE ONE
lines: 还没看见飞机，先听见了：最尽头那座机库的大门往两边滑开，钢轨隆隆地响，引擎怠速的低鸣从靴底爬上来。
门缝越拉越宽：先是一截上翘的机翼，薄得像刀背；再是整副机身，通体雪白，一道深蓝细漆从机头拉到机尾。
高高的尾翼上，四个银色字母：VALE。每一个都比他人还高。一条深红地毯从舷梯铺到车门前，不差一寸。
开胶的靴头踩上红毯。梯下一排深蓝制服齐齐欠身：“早上好，Vale先生。”第一次有人看着他的脸叫这个姓。
舱门在身后合拢，“嗵”的一声，引擎轰鸣被隔成远处的低吟。厚羊毛地毯吞掉了他的脚步。
浅灰麂皮舱壁，胡桃木台面亮得照出他的胡茬。奶白小羊皮座椅，扶手缝着深蓝线，和机身那道漆同一个颜色。
后舱滑门半开：一张铺好的床，一间大理石浴室。他那间漏雨的阁楼整个搬进来，还空得出一截过道。
昨天他错过地铁，没人多看他一眼。今天这架飞机为他晚到的三分钟空转烧油。他站在过道里，没敢坐。

zh: 上个月为了省两块九的地铁钱，我走了四十分钟去见客户。现在一架飞机为我空转着烧油。没人白烧这个油——账单早晚会到。
也许正因为这样，他们才需要你。

zh.title: 造型
zh.hint: 私人助理把一排移动衣架推进过道，三套衣服挂得笔挺，防尘袋还带着熨烫过的余温。落地时，舷梯下会有镜头。

then: 黑色羊毛西装顺着他的肩背垂下来，宽肩被收得利落，连下颌那层胡茬都像是故意留的。
Roman的视线从挺括的领口一路扫过宽肩，落到袖口露出的那截手腕，停了一秒。
奶油色的西装在舷窗透进来的冷光下亮得晃眼，衬得他晒黑的脖颈和粗硬的胡茬，更像个专门来惹事的人。
太显眼。镜头会第一个找到你。
深灰的针织套装松松地贴着身，袖子照旧被他推到小臂，露出结实的腕骨和一截青筋。

zh: 我这辈子坐过最好的位子，是红眼航班的紧急出口排。多出来那十公分伸腿的地方，我当时还挺感激。
Roman在他对面坐下，膝盖几乎抵着他的膝盖。他打开一只深色的鳄鱼纹皮盒，搭扣“咔哒”一响，把东西一样样摆上桌，稳得像在拆弹。

zh.title: 继承包裹
zh.txt: 金属黑卡 · 顶层公寓产权 · 私人航空凭证 · 董事会投票凭证 · 深蓝珐琅家族袖扣 · 黄铜金库钥匙

zh: 盒里衬着深蓝丝绒，每样东西都卡在各自的凹槽里，像早就量好了尺寸，只等他来认领。
航空凭证上印着他的照片。不是证件照，是他在街角买咖啡时被人抓拍的侧脸，夹克领子都没翻好。
黑卡沉甸甸的，是金属的，边缘冰凉。上面几乎什么都没有，只有一行凸印的名字：ADRIAN VALE。
他用拇指擦过那个陌生的姓，粗糙的指腹磨过凸起的字母，像在摸别人身上的疤。
拿着它的那一秒，我是真想要，想得手心发烫。然后我想起来：这世上没有白给的东西，越贵越不是。
没有什么有意义的额度。
因为你还在用昨天只有32美元的方式理解它。
一夜之间，他名下的数字变了，他却没变——还是那个月底要掰着手指算房租的人。
Adrian拿起那把黄铜钥匙。比想象中重，齿纹又深又密，在他的大手里很快被焐热，带着一股旧金属的酸涩气味。
你父亲拒绝放进任何线上系统的东西。
接着是家族袖扣：深蓝的珐琅底，嵌着一枚银色的盾形纹章。Roman看到它的瞬间，眼神停住了。很短，Adrian还是抓到了。
他的目光还钉在那枚袖扣上。食指在桌沿敲了一下，又停住。
你每次说‘没什么’都特别明显。

zh.title: 谜团：袖扣
zh.txt: 金库钥匙已获得。那枚深蓝袖扣让Roman的眼神停了一秒——他不肯解释。

t: roman
那枚袖扣我见过一次，在我父亲的旧徽章旁边。一样的深蓝，一样的纹章。不能是今天。

zh: 飞机爬升，穿进云层。舷窗外先是一片湿漉漉的白，然后是刺眼的蓝。Roman起身，把平板放进头顶的储物柜。
下一秒，机身猛地往下一沉，像有只巨手攥住了机翼。杯里的水晃出杯沿，泼在胡桃木桌面上。
Adrian脚下一滑，伸手去抓椅背，抓了个空，整个人往前栽。Roman已经转身，一手扣住他腰侧，一手攥住他小臂，硬生生把人拽回面前。
Adrian结结实实撞进他胸口。一米八几的个头砸过来，Roman连晃都没晃一下。
西装外套滑开，衬衫底下肩和胸的轮廓一下清晰起来，硬得像一堵墙。扣在他腰后的手掌又宽又热，几乎盖住半侧腰。
他闻到Roman领口的气味：剃须后冷冽的冷杉味，底下压着一点被体温烘出来的热。
Roman的呼吸没乱。Adrian的乱了一拍，胸口起伏得厉害。他低头看那只还停在自己腰上的手——骨节分明，手背上的青筋还没退下去。

zh.hint: Roman的手还扣在你腰上，隔着衬衫烫得惊人。你贴着他，能听见他的心跳——它比他的表情诚实。
win: Roman的心跳到了{bpm}，比Adrian的{mine}还快，一下一下砸在两人贴着的胸口之间。
他低头，像这才意识到手还在那儿。指尖动了一下，又慢了半秒，才松开。
lose: Roman的心跳只有{bpm}，稳得气人。可那只手还是慢了半秒才松开，指腹在他腰侧拖出一道热。
skip: 那只手慢了半秒才松开，掌心的温度留在他腰上，迟迟不散。

zh: 飞机又晃了一下。Adrian伸手去扶，宽大的掌心整个按在了Roman胸口。隔着一层薄衬衫，心跳一下一下，沉沉地撞着他的手心。
Roman握住他的手腕，没推开。那只手比他的还大一圈，拇指在他掌心停了半秒，枪茧蹭过他的掌纹。

zh.hint: 他的手按在你心口，掌心滚烫，指节分明。你的心跳正在出卖你。

opts.t: （声音压得很低）下次再这样，我就不松手了。
Roman没松手，反而把Adrian的手按得更紧，贴在自己心口，多停了两秒。
then: 两秒，够Adrian数清那几下心跳，也够他看清Roman喉结滚动的样子。

opts.t: Roman立刻松开，退后一步。“坐好，系安全带。”
then: Adrian看见了——他耳后那一小片皮肤，红得发烫。

zh: 泼出来的水洇湿了他一截袖口。他干脆脱下西装外套搭在椅背上，又解开一颗衬衫扣子，把袖口一圈圈挽到手肘。喉结在松开的领口下滑了一下。
没了外套，白衬衫把上半身的线条勾得清清楚楚：宽肩，厚实的胸膛，收紧的腰。挽起的袖口下，小臂的肌肉随着动作起伏。
敞开的领口里，锁骨下那道旧疤露出了一截，颜色比周围的皮肤浅，像一道没说完的话。
看就看了。外套是他自己脱的。

zh.hint: 被他抓了个正着。那双灰眼睛就那么等着你，不躲，也不放过。

opts.t: 我已经在往上看了。
then: Roman耳后那片皮肤红了一点。他偏过头，下颌线绷得锋利。
你现在一直这么不要脸？
opts.rthink: 该把扣子扣回去。手抬到领口，又放下了。他看的那个地方，好像不是疤。

opts.t: Adrian把视线甩向窗外的云。太快了，快得像心虚。
then: 他低头划着平板，唇边压着极轻的一点笑，没让它散开。
opts.rthink: 那句话自己跑出去的。三年里我一个字都没说漏过，他扭个头，就让我破了功。

opts.t: Adrian抬手，指尖隔着衬衫落在他锁骨下那道疤上：“确认一下伤势。”
then: 布料下的胸肌猛地一绷。Roman立刻扣住他的手腕，没推开，拇指压上他的脉搏，力道一寸寸收紧。
他把Adrian的手从胸口拿开，慢得像舍不得，指腹顺着他的手背拖过去。
opts.rthink: 这道疤除了缝针的医生，没人碰过。他一根指头按上来，比挨那一刀时还站不稳。

opts.t: 十年变化挺大。
then: 我十七岁的时候你就这么说。
opts.rthink: 他说的是肩膀，不是人。也好。人要是真变了，三年前我就不会接这份活。

zh.title: 差一点失控的气流
zh.teaser: 第三次颠簸，舱灯闪了一下。黑暗里他的呼吸就在你耳边——那三秒里发生的事，只有你们两个知道。
then: 第三次颠簸来得毫无预兆。舱灯“啪”地闪了一下，Adrian整个人被甩向舱壁，肩膀重重撞上冰凉的内饰板。
Roman先到。他一手撑住舱壁，小臂的肌肉绷得像钢缆，把Adrian整个圈在自己和墙之间。
近到能数清他的睫毛。Roman的呼吸擦过他耳侧，是热的，带着一点黑咖啡的苦。
Adrian没动。他的手攥住了Roman的衬衫前襟，指节顶着那层布料，攥得发皱。
Roman低头，鼻尖蹭过他的鼻梁，胡茬擦过他的颧骨，停在他嘴唇上方不到一寸。
在想那天在便利店门口，我为什么停了。
他额头抵上来，闭上眼。呼吸乱了一下，又乱了一下。
“叮”——安全带指示灯亮了，一小团橙光落在两个人之间。
Roman退开前，拇指在他腰侧重重按了一下，像盖了一枚章。
下次没有气流，我也不停。

zh: 四万一千英尺。舷窗外是刺眼的白，阳光斜切进主舱，在胡桃木桌面上铺开一条滚烫的金。
奶油色小羊皮座椅晒出淡淡的皮革味，混着现磨咖啡的焦苦。引擎在脚底低低地嗡，震得杯里的冰块轻轻相碰。
两个人都默契地假装刚才那几秒不存在。Roman坐回对面，Adrian也坐下，胸口那口气还没平。
Roman的西装外套还搭在椅背上。白衬衫袖口挽到手肘，小臂青筋起伏；左腕一块素面钢表，表带压着那道发白的旧疤。
左耳的透明耳麦还塞着，细线没进敞开的领口，锁骨下那道疤露出一截。那双灰眼睛此刻很刻意地没在看Adrian。
Adrian陷在对面座椅里，一米八二的骨架把扶手间撑得满满当当。刚换的新衣服熨得笔挺，肩线贴得太服帖，他总想伸手去扯。
很好。半分钟前我的手还按在他心口上，现在得坐这儿假装欣赏云。我是写文案的，不是演戏的。
空乘从前舱过来，托盘上两只白瓷杯。人还没走近，Roman的视线已经先扫了一圈：舱门、舷窗、她托盘底下的手，最后才落到她脸上。
进任何地方，先扫一圈四周，再看人。今早在楼下是这样，十年前也是这样。
我的黑咖啡，不加糖。……他的加两包糖。
Adrian一个字都还没说。他接过杯子抿了一口，糖已经化开了，甜度分毫不差。
你什么时候开始喝这种苦东西了？以前你兜里永远揣着薄荷糖。
糖也戒，人也戒。你这十年挺有毅力。
Roman的下颌一收，咬肌在胡茬底下绷出一道硬棱。他一紧张就这样，十八岁就这样。
桌上的继承平板正好亮了，冷白的光打在两人之间。一行红字：航程过半，落地前须完成二次身份认证。
记忆认证。今早有人能黑进你楼里的监控，指纹和人脸，信托就不全信了。
双向的。先问我你的事，再问你我的事。确认你是你，也确认护送你的人没被换掉。
所以我的隐私三年前就没了，今天只是走个流程。
第一题弹出来，字体干净得近乎冷酷：Adrian真正紧张的时候，会做什么？
Adrian低头。他的右手不知什么时候已经扣在左手腕上，粗糙的拇指正压着那块凸起的腕骨，一下一下地揉。
连他自己都没察觉的小动作。隔了整整十年，Roman还记得，记得像昨天才看过。
该死。他连这个都记得——那他到底还记得多少？

zh.hint: 认证要求双方作答。平板转了个方向，冷光照上你的脸。轮到你确认：对面坐的，确实是Roman。

qs.q: Roman的咖啡怎么喝？
Roman紧张的时候，会怎样？
Roman走进一个地方，第一件事做什么？
十年前，Roman身上是什么味道？

win.title: MATCH {pct}%
win.txt: 四题全对，护送人身份确认。没有人会无意间，把另一个人记得这么细。

win: 平板边缘亮起一圈绿光，映在Roman灰色的瞳孔里，一闪就灭。
剩下那些，是我不在的那几年。
lose: 进度条停在一个不上不下的数字上，闪了两下，才跳出一行小字：匹配度{pct}%，认证通过。Roman扫了一眼，没说话。
可他答Adrian的那道题，一个字都没错。连Adrian紧张时揉的是哪块骨头，他都知道。
skip: Roman越过桌面，输了一串管理员码。问答被跳过，屏幕只剩一行：护送人身份已人工确认。

zh.hint: 认证通过，平板安静下来。机器的题问完了，你自己的还压着十年——挑一个问他，或者一个都不问。

opts.t: 这十年，你最想念什么？
then: Roman停了很久。他望着舷窗外那片白，下颌线绷出一道冷硬的棱，半天才开口。
你骂我的时候。没人敢那样跟我说话。
opts.rthink: 说出口的是第二个答案。第一个在我相册最底下：十七岁，笑得没心没肺。

opts.t: 那天晚上，谁先移开视线的？
then: Roman的下颌猛地绷紧，咬肌在胡茬底下滚了一下。他没反驳。
opts.rthink: 我先移开，是因为再多看一秒，第二天就走不成了。他不知道，我差一点就没走。

opts.t: Adrian把平板扣了过去，什么都没问。
then: Roman盯着那块扣下去的平板，肩膀松了半寸，眼底却有什么东西跟着暗了下去。
opts.rthink: 他不问了，我该松口气。三年来我把每个答案都备好了，他偏偏一题都不要。

zh: 平板“叮”了一声，又自己亮了。认证一过，一段烫金动画从屏幕底部涌上来：继承人欢迎礼遇·个人礼物额度。
你这么一说，我就一定要管了。
礼物页第一件是一块四万美元的表，铂金表壳在渲染图里亮得扎眼。昨天他绝不会点开，今天系统推荐得像推荐一杯咖啡。
可Roman从来不吃价格这一套。Adrian只是想看他高兴——这个念头来得太顺，顺得非常不方便。
清醒点，Adrian。他是来上班的，你是他的工作。

zh.title: 猜他想要的礼物
zh.hint: 最贵的不一定最对。指尖悬在屏幕上——你还记得他多少？

then: Roman解下左腕那块旧钢表，露出底下那道发白的旧疤，横过腕骨内侧。
Adrian替他扣表带。指腹擦过那道疤，皮肤滚烫，底下的脉搏一下下撞着他的指尖。
Adrian把扣环按到底，“咔哒”一声，这才抬眼。
只是想看看戴你身上好不好看。
Roman看了一眼褪色的布面封面，手指停在开裂的书脊上，指节微微发白。
他翻开扉页，十七岁的他用圆珠笔写的名字还在，笔画重得划破了纸。他合上书，很久没说话。
你连我放几包糖都记得。扯平。
Roman把订阅卡收进西装内袋，靠心口那一侧，又用掌心压平了一下。
Roman把袖扣举到灯下，银面上的刻字反出一点冷光。他看了很久，目光却一次次落回桌上那枚Vale家徽袖扣。
同一个工匠。你从哪儿订的？
他的下颌收紧，太阳穴边一根青筋浮了出来。
Roman捏着那副耳机愣了一下，像从没想过自己还有不工作的时候。

items.sub: 便利店门口 · 十七岁
then: Adrian没点任何一件商品，而是把手机里那张模糊的旧照传上去，备注：冲印，胡桃木框，今天送到。
平板弹出订单确认。Roman看清缩略图的那一秒，整个人静住了——十七岁的Adrian蹲在台阶上，十八岁的他嘴角贴着创可贴。
他喉结滚了一下，手指在屏幕边缘停了很久，像在按住什么不让它掉下来。
你不也留着？相册里那张，角度跟这张一模一样。
Roman没否认。他把平板扣在膝上，过了很久才开口，声音低得只够两个人听见。
框子别太新。旧一点的，像放了十年。

zh: Roman从椅背上的西装内袋里摸出一个旧钥匙扣，放进Adrian掌心。黄铜被磨得发亮，边角圆钝，还带着他的体温。
Adrian攥住它。金属硌着掌心的薄茧，那点体温顺着手掌一路烧上小臂。

zh.title: 回忆：他从没扔掉的钥匙扣
zh.txt: 明显在撒谎。黄铜磨成这样，得在掌心里攥上好几年。

zh: Adrian正想问他到底留了多久，裤袋里的手机一震。认证一通过，Vale家族办公室的日程就同步了过来。
置顶那条镶着金边：“依Alexander Vale先生生前安排，您的未婚妻Sienna Reed女士将于今晚18:00抵达顶层公寓。”
附件是一张工作照。齐下巴的深蜜色短发别在耳后，浅绿色的眼睛，象牙白真丝衬衫外面搭一件驼色大衣。
颈间一根细链，坠着一枚印戒，没戴在手上。她站在会议室门口，手里夹着文件，冲镜头的笑得体又短，像还赶着下一个会。
一个我没见过的爹，给我订了个没见过的未婚妻。我连自己的银行账户都还没搞明白。
他把手机转向Roman。Roman只看了照片一眼，没往下翻——像根本不用翻。脸上纹丝不动，搭在桌沿的那只手却停住了，指节发白。

zh.hint: 一个凭空冒出来的未婚妻。比未婚妻更有意思的，是Roman那只停住的手。

opts.t: 漂亮吗？

then.hint: “漂亮吗？”他就是故意的。你知道他在看你怎么答。

opts.t: 不重要。
跟你不配。
then: Adrian愣了一秒，随即笑出声，那笑从胸腔里震出来，又低又哑。

opts.t: Roman伸手把他的手机屏幕按灭。“我会查清楚她来干什么。”

opts.rthink: 他在看我怎么答。Sienna Reed我认识七年了。她要是来，就不是为了嫁人。

opts.t: 我结婚的话，安保也归你管？
then: Roman沉默了两秒。机舱里只剩引擎低沉的嗡鸣。
进你家门的每个人都归我管。包括她。
opts.rthink: 归我管。站在他身后，看他给别人戴戒指——这份差事，三年前我没算进报价。

opts.t: Adrian什么都没问，只盯着Roman停住的那只手。
then: Roman把手收回去，五指慢慢攥成拳，手背上的青筋一根根绷了起来。
看看这只手。嘴上一个字不说，青筋倒是替他全招了。
Adrian没再追问，把这只手记下了。
opts.rthink: 不是因为她。是她一来，七年前的事就要从她嘴里漏出来了。

zh: 前舱传来机长的声音，请他确认落地安保。Roman起身，从椅背上拎起外套穿好，走了两步，又回头。
你六岁的时候还更听话。

zh.txt: 她的照片我早就看过。没提，是不想提前看你点头。

zh: 撤回。三秒后，新消息：落地前别乱动。——发自他的工作号。那桌上这部，又是哪个号？
桌角，Roman那部黑色加密手机的屏幕亮了一下。照片缩略图一闪而过——是十七岁的Adrian，笑得没心没肺。
理智说不该看。另一半脑子说：他背着你看了你三年。“公平”突然成了一个非常顺手的词。
Adrian的手比脑子先动了。宽大的手掌压住那部手机，指腹上还残留着钥匙扣的温度。

zh.hint: 他在前舱，门缝里漏出他压低的声音。手机没锁屏。你大概只有一分钟。

items: 如果他回到Vale家，就说明你失败了。

apps.lockTxt: 需要密码。提示：便利店那晚的日期。
items: 十七岁的Adrian和Roman坐在便利店门口。照片里的Adrian还没学会带刺的笑，Roman也还没学会把情绪藏起来。
保存于十年前。此后每年同一天，被打开过一次。
我应该在今天之前就告诉他。
未发送 · 三年前 / 一年前 / 昨天
导航记录 · 布鲁克林某便利店 · 41次

win: 他把手机放回原位，角度分毫不差，连屏幕上那道舷窗反光都对准了。
他留着那张照片，整整十年。
比照片更危险的是那条草稿：他不是没想过回来，只是一次又一次没回来。
lose: Adrian只看了一眼就把手机扣回桌上，掌心沁出一层薄汗。心跳比偷看本身还响。
可那张十七岁的缩略图，已经印在他眼睛里了。
skip: Adrian把手机推回原位，指尖没碰屏幕。有些事，他想听Roman亲口说。

zh: 前舱门滑开，Roman回来了，带进一股冷气和淡淡的雪松须后水味。桌上的手机角度没变，屏幕亮度却不对。
他的灰眼睛在手机上停了半秒，又移到Adrian脸上。什么都没说，只是那半秒长得像一场审讯。

zh.hint: 他看过你的手机了。放得很仔细，角度一丝不差——仔细得像心虚。

opts.t: Roman和他对视了一秒，喉结滚了一下，什么都没问。
我的手机好看吗？
then: Adrian没眨眼，下巴微微一抬，胡茬底下压着一点笑。
Roman盯了他两秒，鼻腔里哼出一点气音，没再追问。

opts.t: Roman拿起手机，当着他的面设了锁屏密码。
then: 四个数字，他按得很慢，像故意让人看清。Adrian认得——便利店那晚的日期。

zh: Adrian正要开口，那部黑色手机又亮了。未知号码，语音消息，00:06。红点在屏幕角落一跳一跳。

zh.title: 语音消息 · 未知号码
zh.txt: 电流刮擦般失真的声音，冷得没有一点人味：“Cross，离他远点。”

zh: Roman整个人的气场变了。肩背绷直，眼神沉下去——不是害怕，是猎犬嗅到了血。
他拇指一划，语音被掐断。手背上青筋暴起，指节死死压在屏幕上，快得几乎带出风声。
快得更像是不想让Adrian听见。人藏东西只有两种原因：怕伤到自己，或者怕伤到你。
Cross——Roman的姓。可从小到大，所有人都叫他Roman。会只用一个姓来喊他的，像在喊一个代号。
（Cross是Roman的姓。在他做的那一行里，名字是给熟人的；姓，是给代号和档案的。）

zh.hint: 他把语音掐了。你甚至没听清那个声音是男是女。

opts.t: 再放一遍。
opts.rthink: 再放一遍，他就会问Cross是谁。那个名字底下埋着七年，我还没想好从哪儿挖。

opts.t: 它叫你Cross。它认识你。
then: Roman没回答。耳麦里传来细碎的电流声，他抬手按住，像按住一道伤口。
opts.rthink: 叫我Cross的人，活着的不超过五个。其中一个，知道我今天在这架飞机上。

opts.t: Adrian伸手，宽厚的掌心整个覆住他握着手机的那只手。
then: Roman的手指僵了一下。掌心底下那只手背滚烫，青筋在Adrian手里突突地跳。他没抽走。
opts.rthink: 他的掌心比我的手还烫。我该抽开——抽开，才算听了那句话。我没抽。

t: roman
“离他远点。”七年前，也有人这么跟我说过。上一次，我听了——然后用七年来后悔。

zh: 飞机开始下降，耳膜一阵发胀。纽约从云层底下浮上来，灰蓝的楼群扎在正午的阳光里，像一片竖起的刀。
Roman起身扣好西装扣，把耳麦往耳道里又压了压。这一刻他不像谁的发小，像一堵会走路的墙。
舱门打开以后，站我左边。
因为外面有四十七张媒体证。
舱门还没开，声音先到了。隔着机身，外面是一片闷闷的轰响，像隔着一堵墙听整座球场在吼。
舱门一开，那声音整个灌进来：快门连成一片，几十个嗓子喊着同一个姓——“Vale！这边！Vale先生！”
然后才是光。警戒线外黑压压一片人，长焦镜头像一排架起的枪口；闪光灯一层层炸开，白得发烫，把舷梯扶手照得发蓝。
再近一点，话筒越过警戒线伸到舷梯底下。正午的热风卷着航空煤油和热沥青味，扑了他一脸。
今早七点，他还在布鲁克林拍一台卡住的咖啡机，整栋楼没人记得他姓什么。现在四十七台相机，在等他走下这几级台阶。
写了五年文案，天天求人多看一眼。现在全纽约都在看，我只想找条门缝钻回去。
Roman向前半步，用整副肩背挡在他侧前方，一只大手落到他后腰。不是轻扶，是扣住。
隔着两层布料，那只手的热度直接烙进来。五指张开，掌根压住他的脊椎，稳得像一枚钉子。
四十七台镜头，他把手放在这儿。这人是来保护我的，还是来要我命的？

zh.hint: 四十七台镜头。你的手扣在他后腰，掌心底下是他绷紧的脊背——这个位置，不在任何安保手册里。

opts.t: （俯身到他耳边）走左边。贴紧我。
Roman把手从他后腰移到肩上，换成教科书式的护送姿势。
then: 隔着西装布料，Adrian反而觉得那只手太规矩了，规矩得让人心里发空。

opts.t: （贴着他耳后）别回头。你一回头，明天头条就是你的脸。
then: 扣在后腰的手收紧了一点，指节隔着衣料硌进他的腰窝。

zh: 温热的气息擦过耳后，Adrian的肩膀本能地绷紧，后颈的汗毛一根根竖了起来。
快门声暴雨一样砸下来。Adrian侧过脸，鼻尖几乎蹭上Roman的下颌，近到能闻见他领口的雪松味。
“时机烂透了。”Adrian咬着牙低声说。记者在喊：“你是Alexander Vale的私生子吗？”“你和Sienna Reed订婚了吗？”
订婚。他自己知道这件事，还不到一个小时。

zh.title: 介入
zh.hint: 四十七台镜头，一个问题比一个狠。后腰那只手还扣着你——你要怎么站在这里？

then: Adrian只是笑了一下，下巴微扬，带着点布鲁克林式的混不吝。那张笑脸，第二天上了六家网站的首页。
扣在他后腰的手松了一点点，Roman的胸膛在他肩后轻轻一沉，像松了口气。
他对着最近的那支话筒说完，嗓音又低又稳，像钉进木头里的钉子，又补了一句——
全场死寂了一秒，然后快门声翻了一倍，像冰雹砸在铁皮屋顶上。
Roman低头看了他一眼，灰眼睛里沉着什么，深得看不见底。
谁告诉你们我今天落地的？
最前排的记者一愣，眼珠下意识往人群后面瞟了一眼。
Roman顺着那道视线看过去，眼神一冷，侧头对耳麦低声说了一句。

then.title: 线索：有人提前放了消息
then.txt: 落地时间和那份婚约，都只有家族内部知道。

then: Adrian一把攥住Roman的手腕往身边一带，手背青筋绷起。Roman愣了半秒，顺势站到他身侧。
闪光灯像炸开一样，白光连成一片。这一张，明天会在所有人手机里。

zh.cap: 周三 12:41 · 舷梯上，他的手扣在你后腰
zh.prompt: Private jet stairs on a bright tarmac, dozens of camera flashes, a tall broad-shouldered man in a black suit with an earpiece shielding a broad-shouldered stubbled dark-haired man in a tailored suit, almost his height, his hand firmly at the other man's lower back, both in their late twenties, press crowd blurred in the foreground, cinematic, no text
then: Roman瞥了一眼照片，喉结动了一下，没让删。

zh: 车门“砰”地合上，把记者和热浪一起关在外面。冷气扑面，真皮座椅凉得发硬。
口袋里的手机开始失控地震，几十条，几百条，震得他大腿发麻。

zh.txt: Vale继承人现身，身边跟着神秘保镖。
cm: 这手放的位置也太离谱了。
他根本就是把人往自己怀里带。
没有保镖会这样看雇主。

zh: 放大后的照片比当时更暧昧。Roman的手指陷在他后腰的布料里，而照片里的自己往Roman那边偏着，一点都不像想躲。
互联网认识他们才十一分钟，就已经比他们两个都坦诚。
四万八千个赞。照片里往他身上偏的那个人是我——回头得找个理由，比如风大。
对面，Roman的动态刷新了：一张没有人的照片，酒店电梯的监控视角，灰白、冷硬。配文只有一句：镜头太多了。
Adrian抬眼。Roman正低头看平板，侧脸被车窗外的光切成明暗两半，耳麦线贴着脖颈，像什么都没发过。

zh.hint: 你可以在他的动态下面留言。半个纽约都在看——而他就坐在你对面，一臂之外。

opts.t: 哪一台拍得最好？
then: 评论发出去三秒，私聊就弹了出来。对面那人连头都没抬。
Adrian没删。他把手机往腿上一扣，冲Roman挑了挑眉。
opts.rthink: 最好的那台在东侧第三排，长焦，拍到他往我这边偏。原图我已经让人买下了。

opts.t: Adrian给那条动态点了个赞，什么都没写。
then: 小红心刚亮，私聊就来了。对面Roman的拇指还停在屏幕上。
opts.rthink: 那颗红心挂在我主页上，四万八千人都看得见。我让他取消，自己先截了图。

opts.t: Adrian把那张媒体照存进了私人相册。
then: 没发，没赞，只是存了下来。他的拇指在照片里那只扣住他后腰的手上停了很久。
对面的Roman正在检查路线，眉心压出一道竖纹，完全不知道。
opts.rthink: 绕公园要多四分钟，够人调两次焦。别想那张照片了，Cross。看路线。

zh: 私人电梯从地库直上顶层，一层不停。楼层数字往上跳，Roman从西装内袋抽出一条黑领带，不照镜子，三两下系好，推到喉结底下。楼上有Vale家的人等着交接。
镜面里的Adrian一米八二，新西装绷在宽肩上，领口被他扯开一颗扣，下巴两天没刮的胡茬。脚上还是那双磨秃了头的旧工装靴。
左手腕上，那块二手电子表的塑料表带还缠着黑胶布。整个轿厢里，只有它和这双靴子是他自己花钱买的。

zh.title: VALE 顶层
lines: 数字跳到顶，轿厢轻轻一沉。感应器扫过他的手机，面板浮出一行字：欢迎回家，ADRIAN VALE。
“叮。”门向两边滑开。先撞进眼里的是远处：一整面落地窗，中央公园平得像绿绒布，哈德逊河亮成一条白线。
再近一点，是光。下午三点的太阳砸进来，把二十米长的橡木地板烧成一条金色的河，一直流到他靴尖前。
然后才是屋子本身：双层挑高，黄铜吊灯比他的床还大；一缸白色晚香玉甜得发沉，地毯厚得吞掉脚步声。
他在布鲁克林那间漏雨的阁楼，连同楼下的投币洗衣房整个搬进来，也塞不满这间客厅的一个角。
Adrian站在玄关没动。靴底还粘着布鲁克林的灰，在白色大理石上印出半个淡淡的鞋印。
第一个念头是想要，想得喉咙发紧。第二个念头跟得很快：这么多窗，这么多门——一个人守得过来吗？

zh: 行。脚底下这块大理石，八成比我一年的房租还贵。别乱踩。
Roman从他身侧走过去，寸头贴着头皮，透明耳机线绕在左耳后。他的灰眼睛把客厅扫了一遍，像在给每扇窗算射界。
Adrian笑出一声，嗓音低哑。他跟着Roman往里走，一间间看过去：书房、酒窖、能停下一架直升机的露台。
主卫门口一摊水，从淋浴间那头渗过来，在黑色大理石上亮得看不见。Adrian的靴底一滑，一米八二的人整个朝后栽了下去。
Roman从身后一把圈住他。一只大手死死扣在他腰侧，另一条胳膊横过胸口，小臂硬得像铁杠，把他整个人拽了回来。
两个高个子男人撞在一起，胸膛贴着后背。隔着两层布，Adrian分得清哪一下心跳不是自己的。Roman领口是雪松的味道。
Adrian没动。他反而往后靠了一点，宽肩压进Roman的胸口——就一点，试试。身后那口气，猛地卡住了。
Roman沉默了两秒，扣在他腰上的手指收紧一下，才松开。走廊那头有人敲门框，他退开半步，下颌绷得像什么都没发生。
那只手比十年前大了一圈，也稳了一圈。见鬼。……往后靠那一下，就算是滑倒的。
交接的人退出去，物业经理临走留了一句：主卫的花洒阀门在漏，师傅明早才到。顶层安静得能听见冰箱压缩机的嗡鸣。
Roman把耳机按回耳道，扯平袖口，转身去做下一轮检查。宽背挡掉走廊一半的光，皮鞋落在橡木地板上，一声，一声，像在倒数。

zh.title: 新关系目标
zh.txt: 让Roman为了你，而不是为了工作，主动留下来一次。

zh.title: 关系目标
zh.hint: 黑卡能刷开这层楼的每一扇门，刷不开他的。那双黑皮鞋已经走到门口了。

then: 你能留一下吗？不是工作。
Roman停在门口，宽阔的肩膀顿了一下，才回过头。逆着走廊的光，那双灰眼睛看不出深浅。

then.hint: 他说，不是工作。你手里有十个工作上的理由可以拒绝，一个都没拿出来用。

opts.t: ……我先查完卧室。
行。
then: 你问的是能不能，没问多久。

opts.t: Roman抬手，摘下左耳的耳机，透明线圈垂在白衬衫领口边。

then: Vale先生的安保主管说，他得先查卧室。
嘴上顶回来，那双皮鞋却钉在原地，一寸都没挪。下颌线绷得死紧。
Roman的下颌动了一下。从耳根到短发底下的后颈，慢慢烧了起来。

zh: 主卧朝西。最后一截夕阳从纱帘缝里漏进来，在深灰色的亚麻床品上切出一道橘红的刀口。
能藏东西的地方，都归我管。
Roman反手带上门——关上门，才听得出窗缝漏不漏风。锁舌“咔”地咬进去，客厅的声音一下被切断。十年来第一次，门里只剩他们两个。
Roman脱下西装搭在椅背，扯松领带，解开袖扣，把白衬衫一折折挽到手肘。小臂上青筋鼓着，手腕内侧那道旧疤露了出来。
他一样样查过去：窗锁、通风口、床头灯底座。指节敲在玻璃上，声音闷而实。弯腰时，腰后的枪套在衬衫下压出一道硬线。
Adrian坐在床沿，手肘撑着膝盖，十指交握，看那双大手在自己的房间里一寸寸摸过去。
十年了，这人进门还是先找出口。当年也是——第二天一早，他就用上了。

zh.hint: 门关着，锁舌咬死了，没人会进来。十七岁那晚没做完的事，终于有了一个够大的房间。他就站在一臂之外。

opts.t: Adrian站起来，一只大手攥住他松开的领带。
then: 丝质领带在Adrian的指节间勒紧，Roman被迫低下头。两张脸只隔一掌，他颈侧那根血管突突直跳，清楚得能数。

then.hint: 你的领带缠在他拳头里，他的指节抵着你的喉结，呼吸打在你下巴的胡茬上。你只要再低一寸。

opts.t: 现在多说一句，我会后悔。
then: Roman的拇指按在他手腕内侧，压着那里的脉搏停了一秒，才一点一点松开。

opts.t: Roman低下那一寸，嘴唇在他额头上压了一下，很重，很短。然后才松开领带。
then: 那一点温度在Adrian额头上停了很久，比领带上的褶子还难消。

opts.t: Roman握住他的手，一根一根掰开他的手指，退后一步。
then: 黑领带上留下一道被攥皱的褶，像一道还没愈合的口子。

opts.rthink: 领带在他拳头里，我只要低一寸。三年守则第一条：不碰雇主。我在心里念了第二遍。

opts.t: Adrian往前一步，胸口结结实实贴上他。不是撞到，是故意。
then: Roman僵了一瞬，没退。隔着两层衬衫，两副胸膛的热度撞在一起，他的呼吸一下沉了下去。
Adrian盯着Roman的嘴。那张嘴抿成一条线，下唇有一道很浅的旧裂口。
Roman的呼吸终于乱了一拍，喉结狠狠滚了一下。他没碰Adrian，也没退。
opts.rthink: 退不了。我能在楼顶趴六个小时不动，这会儿却连后退半步的命令都下不出去。

opts.t: Adrian伸手，粗糙的指腹探进他松开的领口，碰了碰锁骨下那道旧疤。
then: 他握住Adrian的手腕，从自己胸口拿开。那么大的一只手，动作却轻得过分。
opts.rthink: 这道疤是那七年留的。再往下一寸还有一道，那一道，我连谎都还没编好。

opts.t: Adrian一把扣住他的后颈，吻了上去。
then: 第一秒，Roman没动，全身绷得像拉满的弓。第二秒，他的手掌扣住Adrian腰侧，把最后一点空隙拉没。
他回应了一下，只有一下。短、重，胡茬磨过胡茬。然后他硬生生停住，额头抵着Adrian。
你不知道自己在干什么。
十年前没干完的事。我清楚得很。
Roman睁开眼，灰眼睛暗得发沉，目光落在他嘴唇上，挪不开。
十年前我停了。现在也得停。
opts.rthink: 十年前停，是怕毁了他。现在停，是怕停不下来。他嘴里一股薄荷味——我戒掉的那种。

opts.t: 查完了，别走。
then: Roman的手停在窗锁上。床头灯照出他下颌一层青茬。这一次，他没有马上拒绝。
六点Reed小姐到，电梯得我放行。
Roman看了一眼腕上的钢表，拉过那把搭着他外套的椅子，坐下了。
二十分钟。剩下的归工作。
opts.rthink: 二十分钟是算过的。电梯放行要三分钟，剩下十七分钟，我一秒都不打算浪费在窗锁上。

zh.title: 卧室门关上之后
zh.teaser: 天黑透了，床头灯是房间里唯一的光。他没有走，领带松了一半。
then: 窗外的天一点点暗下去，曼哈顿的灯一层层亮起来。床头灯是房间里唯一的光，昏黄，把影子拉得很长。
Roman没有走。他站在床沿前，Adrian坐着，膝盖抵着他的膝盖。羊毛西裤磨过羊毛西裤，沙沙一声。
Roman抬手，粗糙的指背很慢地擦过他耳后。十年前，他的拇指停过的同一个位置。
这里。那天我碰的是这里。
我记得的，比你以为的多。
他弯下腰，一只手撑在Adrian身侧的床沿，床垫陷下去一块。他的额头抵上Adrian的额头。
呼吸缠在一起，热的，带着一点薄荷牙膏的凉。谁都没有再往前那半寸。
Adrian没说停。他一把攥住Roman胸前的衬衫，布料在拳头里皱成一团，把人往下拽了一点。
Roman的嘴唇擦过他的嘴角，停住。他闭上眼，眉心拧着，撑在床沿的那只手青筋暴起，在跟自己较劲。
他的手在抖。全副武装、能徒手卸枪的Roman Cross，手在抖。
耳机里刺啦一声电流：“B区巡检完毕。”
过了很久，Roman才直起身，拇指在他下唇上重重按了一下，像盖一个章。

zh: Roman先退开半步。不是逃，更像把选择权还给Adrian。他抬手整理领带，粗大的指节在丝面上抚了两遍，比平时慢。
如果还要继续这样，我们得有规则。

zh.title: 约束区
zh.hint: Roman把选择权推回你手里。你定下的规则，这个男人会一条条照做，像执行命令。

items.t: 公开场合保持职业关系
then: Roman没回答，嘴角往下压了压，没压住。
你说的暧昧，范围有多大？
Roman认真点头，眉头微皱，像在背一条安保条例。
那现在，我可以帮你把领口扣好吗？
你确定要把这条写进规则？

zh: 五点四十，Roman去主卫查那只漏水的阀门。半分钟后，里面“嘭”一声闷响，接着是水砸在瓷砖上的轰鸣，和一句压得很低的脏话。
Adrian冲过去。阀芯崩飞了，水柱横着喷，Roman单膝跪在一地水里，一只大手死死压着出水口，从头到脚湿透。
别跟它较劲。总阀在洗手台底下。
他拉开柜门，单膝跪进水里，摸到那只铜阀，一拧到底。水声断了。布鲁克林的房东从来不接电话，这活儿他闭着眼都会。
这句话落在湿透的瓷砖上，谁都没去捡。Roman去客卫冲掉一身脏水，换上车里备用包中的衣服。门再打开时，一团白色热气先涌了出来。
Roman头发湿着，短发根根立起，发梢挂着水珠。黑T恤还潮着，黏在肩膀和胸口上，勾出一块块结实的起伏。
灰色运动裤，光脚踩在地板上，毛巾搭在颈后。一滴水顺着颈侧滑下来，经过喉结，钻进领口。
看就看了。阀门是他拧爆的，湿成这样不归我管。

zh.hint: 他抓到你在看。湿T恤贴在他身上，水珠还在往下滚。规则里，确实没写这一条。

opts.t: 规则里没写不能看。
then: Roman抬眼，灰眼睛隔着湿漉漉的额发，看了他整整两秒。
opts.rthink: 备用包里明明有衬衫，我先套的是T恤。他以为我是没得选。

opts.t: Adrian走过去，扯下他颈后的毛巾，替他擦头发。
then: Roman僵住了，低着头，任他擦。毛巾底下，短发扎着掌心，热气一阵阵往上冒。
opts.rthink: 毛巾底下，他看不见我的脸。也好。我现在这副表情，不该让任何雇主看见。

zh.title: 大堂来电
zh.txt: 礼宾台：Reed小姐已到，日程18:00。是否放行私人电梯？

zh: Roman一把抓过手机，点开电梯监控。画面里，一个女人独自站在黑胡桃木轿厢里，抬头冲镜头点了一下，像知道是谁在看。
他三两下套上备用的白衬衫，扣子一路扣到顶，湿发往后一捋，快得像在清理现场。
“叮。”电梯门滑开。Sienna走出来，齐下颌的深蜂蜜色短发，浅绿色的眼睛，象牙白真丝衬衫外面一件剪裁利落的驼色大衣。
颈间一根细链，坠着一枚家徽戒指。鞋跟不高，走路几乎没声音，手里一只酒红色皮质公文包，身上一点很淡的无花果香。
像刚从董事会下来，顺路过来一趟。她第一眼看Adrian，从工装靴看到胡茬，像在核对一份尽调报告。第二眼落在Roman身上——停得太久，不像第一次见。
她走近，替Adrian理了理敞开的领口，指尖在锁骨附近停了一秒。颈间那枚戒指荡下来，冰凉的金属贴上他的皮肤。
Roman没走近，也没打断。垂在身侧的手慢慢握成拳，手背上青筋一根根顶起来，指节泛白。
行，我是道具。她理的是我的领子，量的是他的拳头。

Adrian翻到最后一页。签名栏里，墨水早就干透了：ADRIAN VALE。
有人让我拿着它来，演一个称职的未婚妻。可我看过最后一页。
Roman伸手拿过文件。看到签名的一瞬，他瞳孔猛地一缩，捏着纸边的手指发白，随即恢复如常。
他认得这笔字。Roman看那行签名的样子，像在认一具尸体。

zh: 夜里的顶层是另一副样子。灯全灭了，只剩地脚灯一线冷白。落地窗外，整座城的灯火铺成一片烧不尽的炭。
Sienna九点才走。晚饭是她点的外卖——“Vale家的厨子会把菜单报给Evelyn。”Roman坚持亲自送她下地库。电梯门合上前，她伸手按住，压低了声音。
你该问问他，七年前去了哪儿。
那点无花果香在玄关散了很久。Adrian靠在卧室门框上，拇指一下下摩挲着左手腕那块缠着黑胶布的电子表。

zh.hint: 他人还在地库。响了三声，他自己挂了。

roman

还有下午那几条规则——不是管你的。是管我的。

skip: Adrian盯着那条红色的未接来电，没回。四分钟后，玄关门禁轻轻一响，Roman回来了，带着一身地库的凉气，一个字没提。

zh: 群里安静得反常。客厅另一头，Roman忽然按住耳机，压低声音重复了一遍：“东侧楼顶，反光。确认。”
Roman整个人一下变了。背脊绷直，右手无声地移到腰后，下颌的肌肉一棱一棱绷出来。

zh.hint: 耳机里那句话还在响。你不能告诉他为什么——但你得让他退进卧室，锁上那扇门，现在。

opts.t: Roman转进走廊，避开他的视线，拨通了Adrian的电话。
then: 三秒后，Adrian的手机在掌心里震起来：ROMAN来电。他皱着眉接起。

opts.t: Roman大步过来，一手按着他胸口把人推进卧室，带上门。“锁上。现在。”
Roman只发了一条消息：进屋，锁门。别问为什么。
then: Adrian回得很快，拇指几乎砸在屏幕上：为什么？
一个永远冷静的人开始紧张时，恐惧才会传染。Adrian听见自己的心跳，一下下撞在耳膜上。

else.hint: 他明明就在同一层。声音少了房间的回响，低沉、贴耳，带着一点压不住的喘。

总比隔着客厅喊强。

听我说。进卧室，把门锁上。

现在别问。锁上了，再问。

窗帘别拉开。陌生号码，一个都别回。

我就在走廊这头。哪儿也不去。

zh: Adrian退进卧室，拧上门锁，金属锁舌“咔哒”一声落定。屏幕上方又弹下一条彩信。未知号码，三张照片。
前两张，是顶层的窗。第三张一格一格加载清楚：Roman站在电梯外，白衬衫，侧脸冷硬——就是今晚这身。拍摄角度，来自一个本不该有人的高处。
一粒红色的激光点，稳稳压在他左胸，压在心脏的位置。下面一行字：明天一个人来。否则，你的保镖会先死。
东侧楼顶。镜头对着他至少半小时，扳机一下没扣——他们要的是我，不是他。行。那就来拿。

zh.txt: 上一次有人叫我离你远点，我听了。这次不听了。

zh: 撤回。三秒后，新消息弹出来，短短四个字：你还好吗？
一整天，他都在追问Roman这十年去了哪儿。现在他只想确认一件事：明天，那粒红点不会再落回那件白衬衫上。

t: roman
他没回消息。他一紧张就去摸左手腕，摸那块缠着黑胶布的破电子表。现在一定在摸。

zh: 拇指悬在屏幕上。接下来这一下，决定他是把Roman挡在身后，还是拉到身边。
en: 7:12 a.m., and the Brooklyn sky is the color of dishwater. The radiator clanks twice and coughs up heat that smells like rust. The window is fogged solid.
The cheap coffee maker has jammed again, red light blinking. The washer hits spin and starts punching the wall, walking a mug toward the edge of the counter one shudder at a time.
The faucet won't quite shut. Drip. Drip. Onto last night's takeout box, lid curled open, the cold noodles fused into one brown brick under a skin of sauce.
He's been up since 6:15, when the slippers went slapping down the stairwell — Mrs. Ortiz from 3B, going down for her paper. Three years, and she has never been a minute early or late.

A bag of trash hangs off the doorknob. Last week Hector, the super, chained the back door shut from the inside with a bike lock — "for the junkies" — so taking out the garbage now means going out the front and around half the block.
His phone lights up, cold white in the gray room. Two notifications: CHECKING — $32.18. RENT DUE FRIDAY.
Adrian is six feet even, barefoot on cold tile. The gray T-shirt has been washed to a stretched-out collar, but his shoulders still pull it tight, the cotton straining across his shoulder blades.
Two days of dark stubble on a hard jaw. Sweatpants slung low on his hips. On his wrist, a secondhand digital watch, the cracked plastic strap held together with black electrical tape.
He lifts one big hand and slams the heel of it into the side of the machine — bang — the veins on the back of his hand standing up one by one. The thing chokes, then finally starts to drip.
Phone wedged between shoulder and jaw, stubble rasping against the glass. His boss's voice squeezes out of the speaker: the client changed direction. Start over. All of it.
Start over. Easy for him to say. I do math before I make a second pot of coffee.
That morning, I had thirty-two dollars in checking.
Ten years ago. Night rain melts the convenience-store neon into puddles of trembling red and green. Water sheets off the plastic awning. The air smells like wet asphalt and hot-case food.

Seventeen-year-old Adrian crouches on the step, jacket soaked to his back, his own knuckles split — they took that fight together. He tears a bandage open with his teeth and presses it to the cut at the corner of eighteen-year-old Roman's mouth.
Roman's knuckles are raw and fresh, blood thinning in the rain. He doesn't make a sound. He just watches Adrian's fingers, breathing hard — spearmint and copper.
They look up at the same time. Too close. Roman's thumb grazes the spot behind his ear — rough, burning hot. The rain goes very far away. Half an inch.
It never landed. Half an inch. Next day I told myself it was the rain, that he'd taken one to the head. I've been telling myself that for ten years. The skin behind my ear has never bought it once.
The next morning, he was gone. Adrian sent three texts. He typed half of a fourth and deleted it. After that he'd walk two blocks out of his way rather than pass that store.
About his father, his mother only ever said one thing: It's complicated. She always said it while drying a plate that was already dry.
Adrian swallows that and the ten-year hole together and shoulders onto the rush-hour train — wet parkas, cheap cologne, somebody else's coffee.
I thought that was my life. Revisions, rent, standing between other people's elbows all the way to the last stop.
Brakes shriek, tires screaming on wet asphalt. Three black SUVs stop dead outside the old building, paint so glossy the whole shabby street is reflected in it.

en.hint: Three cars have just pulled up downstairs when your phone rings. Unknown number.
lines: roman
…Adrian.
roman
Don't hang up. Look out the window.
roman
Second car. I'm waiting downstairs.
roman
Eight-oh-five. I'm not coming up — you come down.
then: The line goes dead. Nobody has said his name like that in ten years, and it takes him half a second to know the voice.
skip: Adrian declines the unknown number. Three seconds later, downstairs, the door of the second car opens.

en: Roman steps out from behind the second car. Black suit. Earpiece. The wet wind can't move a single hair on his head. Ten years.

en.t: THE HEIR HE CAME BACK FOR

en: His boss's last text is still on screen: Need revision before noon. Adrian rams the sticking glass door with his shoulder. The hinge groans.
Faded olive field jacket. Jeans worn white at the knees. Work boots with the soles starting to peel, laces knotted any old way.
Canvas bag slung across one broad shoulder, the old laptop inside still whining its fan. Cold coffee in one fist, the trash bag in the other, last night's marker ink smudged across his knuckles.
First, the sound. Three big engines idling on the same low note, the manhole cover under his boots humming with it.

Then the cars. Three black SUVs, nose to tail, blocking half the street. Windows tinted all the way down, paint so glossy it looks wet, throwing the whole block back at him — rusted fire escapes, tipped-over trash cans, and him.
The curb that's always jammed with delivery bikes has been swept clean. The deli guy across the street stands frozen in his doorway with a mop. Even the pigeons have backed up onto the ledge.
First thought: whose money do I owe, and how much, to rate three of these.
He sets the trash bag down on the step, slow, and frees his right hand. Grow up on a street like this and you learn it early: free a hand first.
The second door opens. Roman checks the street before he looks at anyone — rooftops, windows, the corner. His jaw locks when he's tense. Adrian knows all of it.
He recognizes him too fast, and that's what pisses him off. His brain needs a second. His body doesn't — his gut drops, the paper cup crumples in his fist, and cold coffee runs between his knuckles.
Roman straightens up, six-two, and makes the doorframe look small. Black suit cut close to the body. No tie. White shirt open one button at the throat.
At eighteen Roman was all elbows, a plank nobody had sanded. Now the suit takes its shape from his shoulders, and his chest could block half the car door.
Polished shoes that cross a puddle without throwing a drop. A plain steel watch on his left wrist — and under the band, a pale old scar it doesn't quite cover.
Hair buzzed close, a dark shadow over his skull. A jaw like it was cut with a blade, rough with stubble. Behind his left ear, the earpiece wire disappears under his collar.
Then the eyes. Gray, like thin ice on a winter river. The second they land on Adrian's face, the ice cracks.
The wind lifts his collar: a scar under the collarbone, paler than the skin around it, like a bolt of lightning somebody stitched shut.
Where the hell have you been for ten years? — No. First: who gave you that scar. Whoever it was, I'll kill him.
Adrian has ten years of questions. His eyes go down anyway and stay on that collarbone one second too long. His Adam's apple bobs.

en.hint: He caught you looking. Ten years, and you're losing round one.

opts.t: Not remotely.
then: Roman's eyes hold on his face for half a second. His throat moves. Then he goes back to cold iron, like it never happened.
opts.rthink: 'Not remotely.' Same drop at the end he used at seventeen when he lied. Three years watching him through a long lens, and today he finally looks back.

opts.t: Adrian turns his head, jaw tight, and develops a deep interest in a license plate.
then: Roman doesn't call it. The corner of his mouth moves — there and gone, quick as wind over a blade.
opts.rthink: Those plates are fake. I swapped them myself last night. He's studying them like scripture, and his ears are red down to the collar.

opts.t: You first. Are you done?
then: His own jaw locks the second it's out. A vein ticks once at his temple.
opts.rthink: Not even close. Ten years wasn't enough. Assessing risk—the biggest one on this street is standing right in front of me, chin up.

en.hint: He's still looking at you, chin up, as stubborn as he was at seventeen. Ten years, and you still don't know which sentence goes first.

opts.t: Get in.
I know you've got questions. Get in first.
then: His voice is steady. The hand on the door isn't — knuckles going white, veins rising across the back of it.

opts.t: Roman reaches for his arm — stops an inch from the jacket — pulls back. "Get in, Adrian."
then: Adrian saw the hand stop. He saw it shake.

en: Ten years, and that's what you open with?
Adrian walks right up to him, boots grinding through a puddle. Not much shorter. Chin up, the muscle in his jaw a hard ridge under the stubble.
Close enough to smell him: cedar, gun oil, a trace of cold smoke. Ten years ago he only ever smelled like spearmint.
He doesn't argue. He opens the back door himself and braces one hand on the frame above it — a stance that could be shielding a man, or cutting off his exit.

en.hint: You rehearsed this for forty minutes in the car until your palms were wet. There's no right way to say it.

opts.t: Your father died yesterday.
Adrian, let me finish. ...Your father died yesterday.
then: He says it slowly, word by word, gray eyes never leaving Adrian's face, like he's waiting for the swing.

opts.t: Roman doesn't say it. He hands over the tablet, the obituary on screen.
then: White on black, cold as a headstone. Adrian reads the headline: ALEXANDER VALE DIES AT 61.

en: For the first time, the sarcasm drains off Adrian's face — like someone yanked away the shield he's held up his whole life.
The street noise pulls away. All he hears is his own heartbeat, slow and heavy, like someone dragging an iron trunk across the floor upstairs.
You do. His name was Alexander Vale.

en.title: Your Father Was Alexander Vale
en.txt: Hotels, banks, airlines, media — half the names on the Manhattan skyline. That Vale.

en: The door shuts with a click like a safe locking. The building, the store, the bus stop slide away behind dark soundproof glass.
The cabin smells of new leather and cold air, so quiet he can hear the vents breathe. His worn-out jeans on cream leather look like a burglar who wandered in.
Roman sits beside him, suit trousers pulled tight over heavy thighs, his knee a fist's width away. Every turn sways his body heat across the gap.
Roman takes a black leather folder from the front seat and sets it on Adrian's knees. His hand stays on Adrian's knee a fraction of a second too long.
Black calfskin, heavier than his old laptop. No words on the cover, just a silver V pressed into the bottom corner, the edges rubbed shiny. Somebody has opened this a lot.
Inside, heavy paper, a watermark showing against the window. Page one: ALEXANDER VALE — DECEASED. Page two: PATERNITY CONFIRMATION. Page three: ADRIAN HALE / 99.998% MATCH.
He skips the assets and reads the DNA result twice, thumb pressed down on the number so hard the nail goes white.
The number is too precise to hide behind 'there's been a mistake.'
No thunder. No soundtrack. His life just got rewritten on one expensive sheet of paper, in a car that is far too quiet.
Twenty-seven years, not one photo. Now he's dead, and suddenly he remembers to drop a paternity test in my lap.
He died yesterday. And today I'm suddenly his son?
You were his son yesterday too.
Roman gives him a few seconds — watches his throat work twice — before he unlocks the tablet: VALE GROUP — CONTROLLING BENEFICIAL HEIR.
At the top of the screen, a card. Matte black, a hairline of gold around the edge, and dead center a number field under a frosted seal. All he can tell is that the number is long.

Below it, a column of logos, one after another: the bank he passes on the train every morning, the hotel by his office he has never once walked into, the row of white tail fins with a V on them at the end of the runway.
He notices his thumb is already resting on the seal. He takes it back and wipes it on his jeans.
Five years writing ads, and I've typed "life-changing" a hundred times. Turns out the real thing looks like this: a box you can't open.
Enough that the number stops helping. Controlling interests. Private aviation. Hotels. Media. Real estate. Banking.
This morning I had thirty-two dollars and eighteen cents.
The bank holding that thirty-two dollars? You own part of it now.

en.hint: A number you haven't even read yet is sitting on your knees, heavy as hot iron. Your first move is—

opts.t: Give me the complete list. No summaries.
then: Adrian pulls the tablet back toward himself and starts swiping fast.
I just prefer being shocked with information.
Roman's mouth twitches, like a fish moving under ice. The screen unfolds: Black Card. Manhattan penthouse. Private aviation. Temporary board vote.
opts.rthink: He wants the full list, not the summary. Good. As long as he doesn't ask who compiled it—I've had it memorized for three years.

opts.t: Did my mother know?
then: For the first time, Roman looks careful. The muscle in his jaw shifts, like he's grinding a sentence he isn't allowed to say.
It's the answer I can give you right now.
She spent her whole life counting bills.
Adrian's fingers press down on the asset page, knuckles standing out, creasing the paper.
Your mother made choices to keep you away from this family.

then.title: Clue: She Knew More
then.txt: For three whole seconds the money stops feeling like a prize — and starts feeling like a door your mother held shut for twenty-seven years.

opts.rthink: She knew more than I'm allowed to say. One more question and I'd have to choose: lie to him, or make him hate her.

opts.t: Adrian jabs his thumb down and kills the asset page.
then: You don't want to see it?
I want to know why you're the one showing it to me. How long?
Roman pauses. Window light strobes across his face, one bar at a time, and never reaches his eyes.
Three years. It hits harder than any number on that page. Money explains the cars. It doesn't explain three years of watching and never once walking over.
opts.rthink: Four point eight billion, killed with one thumb. He never looks at the money first. He looks at the person. I'd rather he looked at the money.

opts.t: Stop the car. I'm verifying this myself.
then: Someone accessed your building cameras at 6:14 this morning.
He slides his encrypted phone across. The black case is still warm from his palm.
Verify the DNA. Verify me. Verify the lawyers. But do it while moving.
Lab receipt. The official Vale obituary. Roman's security clearance. The law-firm filing. Adrian checks every one, his thumb slowing with each. All real.
opts.rthink: Stop? After 6:14 I can't vouch for a single window on this street. If he gets out, I'll haul him back in and take the punch.

en: Roman taps the corner of the tablet with a callused forefinger. The asset page shrinks away. Four black-and-white feeds take its place, snow hissing at the edges.
The part nobody puts in the inheritance brochure. Someone got into your building's cameras at 6:14 this morning. These are the four feeds from that minute.
Most likely. The other possibility is worse.
The air in the car seems to drop two degrees. The hair on the back of Adrian's neck stands up.
This is the moment the inheritance stops being absurd and starts being dangerous.
Four feeds, one timecode: 06:14. Adrian goes through them one at a time.
CAM A, stairwell: an old woman in a bathrobe working her way down, one hand on the rail. Mrs. Ortiz, 3B, going for her paper.
CAM B, front stoop: a delivery guy drops two bags on the step, yawns straight into the lens, and leaves.
CAM C, back door: a man in a work jacket with a toolbox comes up the alley — the radiator guy, by the look of him. He takes the handle, pulls, and the door swings open. He steps inside.
CAM D, lobby: Hector the super, mop and bucket, working the floor.
Nothing, at first glance. One beat-up building, one morning, four completely ordinary people.

en.hint: Roman turns the tablet toward you. "You've lived in that building three years. You'll see what's wrong faster than I will."
en.title: Security feed · 6:14
en.hint2: Clues: Mrs. Ortiz goes down for her paper at 6:15 every day; last week Hector chained the back door shut from the inside. One of these four things cannot happen in that building — tap it.

cams.clue: Mrs. Ortiz heading down for her paper around 6:15 — same as every day for three years.
The delivery guy yawns right into the lens, drops the bags, leaves.
Hector chained the back door from the inside last week. This man pulls it open from the outside — and never shows the camera his face, every step in a blind spot.
Hector mopping the lobby. Business as usual.

win: The back door. Hector chained it from the inside last week. You can't open it from the alley.
Roman turns his head and looks at him — a long look, like confirming something he already knew.
He knows. How the hell does he know what's on our back door?

win.title: Clue Card: Inside Knowledge
win.txt: A chained door that opens for him. Every blind spot, avoided. Whoever this is knows Vale's security system.

win: I let that one go. Pick it up and I'd have to ask why. Ask why, and I'd have to hear the answer.
lose: Roman spreads two fingers and enlarges the back-door feed, his big hand covering half the screen.
Back door's been chained from the inside since last week. Can't be opened from the alley. He just pulled it open.
...How does he know about the chain on our back door?
On screen, the man never once faces the camera. Every step lands in a blind spot.

lose.txt: A chained door that opens for him. Every blind spot, avoided. Whoever this is knows Vale's security system.

lose: I let that one go. Pick it up and I'd have to ask why. Ask why, and I'd have to hear the answer.
skip: The back door's been chained since last week. He pulled it right open, and walked every blind spot. That's why I came myself.

en.why: The man on the feed knows Vale security

t: roman
I flagged that blind spot three years ago. Nobody fixed it. Today somebody used it. Whoever he is — he touches one hair on Adrian's head, and I'll teach him personally what a blind spot is.

en.place: Vale motorcade, en route to the airfield

en: The SUV's windows are tinted so dark the September sun comes through cold and blue-grey. The cabin smells of new leather and cedar, too clean for anyone to have ever lived in it.

Adrian has the window side of the back seat, six feet of him folded into leather built for men who sit still. Army-green jacket washed thin, the grey T-shirt under it stretched out at the collar, work boots splitting at the toe.
He hasn't slept. Stubble has come in dark along his jaw, shadows dug in under his eyes. One big hand rests on his knee, knuckles still pale from gripping something too long.

Roman sits beside him, spine straight as a rifle barrel. Black suit cut close to the body, shoulders broad and squared, white collar points razor-crisp, a clear earpiece in his left ear, its coil vanishing under the collar.
Dark hair clipped close to the skull. Grey eyes fixed on the road, quietly counting every car that slides past. A steel watch on his wrist, and under the band, a pale old scar.
Ten years, and the man sits like a knife in a sheath. Me: a stretched-out T-shirt, two days of stubble, and boots with their mouths hanging open.

then: Three years. The number follows him like a nail in a tire, out of the Brooklyn brownstones and onto a highway still slick with morning fog.
Roman's profile hangs in the tinted glass, perfectly still. Not even the line of his jaw gives.
else: Cup holder. That one's yours. Two sugars.
Adrian looks down. Still hot. Two sugars, no cream. He never said a word about it. If Roman only took this job today, how does he know?
How long have you known about me?

else.hint: He asked. His eyes are nailed to your face, jaw locked, and the only sound is tires hissing on asphalt. You can lie, you can stall, or you can tell him.

opts.t: (half a second of silence) Three years.
...Long enough.
Roman doesn't answer. One swipe of his thumb, and the tablet's cold light catches his knuckles: ASSIGNMENT START DATE. Three years ago today.
then: Adrian stares at the date. His Adam's apple works once. He doesn't say anything for a long time.

en: Three years means Roman knows about the move from Queens to the Brooklyn attic with the leaking skylight. The three jobs. The weekends moonlighting for a moving company, hauling refrigerators up five flights to make rent.
Knows that last winter two guys boxed him in behind a bar, and he took one punch and gave back three, then went home and put six stitches in the back of his own hand in the bathroom mirror.
Knows he rolled an ankle in a pickup game, played out the last round anyway, limped twenty blocks home, and clocked in the next morning like nothing happened.
Being walked out on was simple: you hate the guy, then you slowly forget him. Finding out he was a street away the whole time, watching through a windshield, is harder to swallow.
That night in the alley it was two on one, and I bought the needle and thread at the bodega downstairs. If he was across the street watching, I hope he got a good look: I never once yelled for help.
That night in the alley. Were you 'protecting' me then?
Across the street. By the time I stepped off the curb, you didn't need me.
So you stood there and watched.
Your right hook's heavier than it was at seventeen.
Adrian's jaw locks. Somehow the compliment lands harder than the punch did.

en.hint: Three years across the street — watching you haul freight, take hits, hit back — and he never once crossed over. How do you handle it?

opts.t: Fine. I'll take half of it on faith.
then: Half is more than I've earned.
Roman looks at him for a long time. Something in those grey eyes sinks, then slowly surfaces again.
opts.rthink: Half. Ten years ago he handed me all of it and I dropped it. I'll earn back the rest if it kills me.

opts.t: A good suit doesn't turn stalking into protection.
then: Roman glances down at the knife-pressed front of his suit, then back up, one eyebrow lifting a fraction.
The second half was the point.
opts.rthink: He said the suit looks good. I'll keep that. The rest he's right about—I called myself the same thing that night in the alley.

opts.t: Was it my father?
then: Roman's pupils tighten; a muscle jumps along his jaw. Fast. Adrian catches it anyway.
That was me regretting eye contact.

then.title: Clue: Father May Have Hired Roman
then.txt: Alexander Vale found him three years before he died — earlier than any will.

opts.rthink: Old Vale had one condition three years ago: never let him know who was paying. I just breached it with half a look.

opts.t: So where I drink on Friday nights, and till when — that's in the report too?
then: Roman turns to the window. His throat moves above the starched collar.
The place on Seventh. Third stool from the left. Usually till one-forty.
Adrian laughs — low, rough from no sleep, the sound coming up from deep in his chest.
The bartender comped you three times. Irregular transactions. I log those.
We're coming off the highway. Sit back.
But the hand on his knee has closed into a fist, veins rising one by one across the back of it, his jaw set like he's grinding something to dust.
Irregular transactions. Three free beers from a bartender, and he filed them as irregular transactions. Noted. So the man does have a pressure point.
opts.rthink: The third free round, the bartender put a hand on his shoulder. I rewrote that report four times. All that survived was 'billing irregularity.'

en: Outside, the brick walk-ups and coin laundries fall away, replaced by grey airport service roads, chain-link fence, and rows of blank-faced freight warehouses.
Ten years ago, Roman was right beside him. Then seven years of nothing. Then three years of 'protection' — without ever once showing his face.
Those seven years were cut out of the timeline with a blade. Clean edges. Not one loose thread.
Roman's fingers slowly close on his knee, knuckles rising one by one, crushing creases into the wool.
Roman finally turns his head. Those grey eyes come straight at him, close enough to see what's being held down in them.
A summer night ten years ago, the rain thick and airless. The convenience store's AC unit rattling on the wall, fluorescent tubes buzzing overhead, puddles holding their sick white light.
Eighteen-year-old Roman sat on the floor against the ice chest, lip split, the blood dried dark. His knuckles were skinned raw, the collar of his T-shirt yanked crooked.
Adrian tore the bandage open with his teeth, hands not quite steady. As he pressed it on, they kept leaning closer, close enough to smell rain and rust and mint candy on him.
Roman's thumb brushed behind Adrian's ear, rough and burning. Half an inch between their mouths.
The AC unit kept humming. Rain drummed on the awning. Neither of them moved.
One blink and it's twenty-eight-year-old Roman, less than an arm's length away. Shoulders a full size wider than they were, a frame that fills the suit without a wasted inch.
His voice has dropped into his chest. His collar lifts and settles with each breath, and under the stiff points, the tail end of an old scar shows just below his collarbone.
At seventeen, wanting to kiss him was confusing. At twenty-seven, the problem is clarity — wanting it so precisely his back teeth ache.
Cool it. He's your bodyguard. You pay his salary. Fine — your dead father does.

en.hint: That half inch has been hanging between you for ten years. The only sound is the low breath of the vents. This time — do you move?

opts.t: Adrian reaches over and runs a rough fingertip along the pale scar on his wrist.
then: Roman catches his wrist on instinct — fast as a draw, but gentle, his thumb landing square on Adrian's hammering pulse.
The heat of that palm stays on Adrian's wristbone half a second too long before he lets go.
opts.rthink: This one's nothing. The one that hurts is under my collarbone—I got it the year I left. One more question and I'd have told him everything.

opts.t: The car banks into a turn. Adrian's knee settles against his thigh and stays there.
then: Through the thin suit wool, the muscle in Roman's thigh turns to iron. He looks down, lashes low.
Roman leans back into the leather as if to put distance between them. His knee doesn't move an inch.
That's an answer. Adrian turns to the window so he won't grin.
opts.rthink: I should move. Every muscle in my leg is waiting for the order. I don't give it. I've started counting the turns left on this road.

opts.t: Adrian says nothing. He just watches Roman's mouth.
then: Roman's words slow down. His Adam's apple drags once above that stiff collar.
That's usually when you're most dangerous.
opts.rthink: He's watching my mouth exactly like that night. I stopped then, and I was gone by morning. He still thinks those are two separate things.

opts.t: Later. Inheritance first.
then: Maybe ten years taught me boundaries.
Roman huffs a quiet laugh through his nose.
opts.rthink: He stopped. I should be relieved. But the kid who never hit the brakes at seventeen—I'm the one who taught him how.

en.title: VALE ONE
lines: Before he sees the plane, he hears it: the last hangar's doors rolling apart on rumbling steel tracks, an idling engine's drone climbing up through his boot soles.
The gap widens. First a wing, long and thin, its tip curled up like the spine of a blade; then the whole fuselage, pure white, one deep-blue pinstripe from nose to tail.
High on the tail fin, four silver letters: VALE. Each one taller than he is. A deep red runner is laid from the airstair to the car door and stops exactly there.
His split-toed boots land on the red. At the foot of the stairs a line of navy uniforms bows as one: "Good morning, Mr. Vale." The first time anyone has said that name to his face.
The door seals behind him with a heavy thunk and the engine roar drops to a distant hum. Thick wool carpet swallows his footsteps whole.
Pale grey suede walls, walnut polished enough to show him his own stubble. Cream lambskin seats, the armrests stitched in the same deep blue as the stripe outside.
At the back, a sliding door stands half open on a made-up bed and a marble bathroom. His whole leaking attic would fit in here and still leave room for an aisle.
Yesterday he missed a train and nobody on the platform looked up. Today a jet sits burning fuel for the three minutes he was late. He stands in the aisle and doesn't sit down.

en: Last month I walked forty minutes to a client to save the two-ninety subway fare. Now a jet is idling just for me, burning fuel by the gallon. Nobody burns that for free. The bill's coming.
That's probably why they chose you.

en.title: Styling
en.hint: An assistant wheels a rolling rack down the aisle, three looks hanging razor-straight, garment bags still warm from the steamer. There'll be cameras at the foot of the stairs when they land.

then: The black wool drops clean off his shoulders and tapers hard at the waist; suddenly even the stubble on his jaw looks deliberate.
Roman's gaze travels from the sharp collar across the breadth of his shoulders and down to the inch of wrist at the cuff. It stops there for a second.
The cream suit glows in the cold light from the windows, and against it his sun-dark throat and rough stubble make him look like a man who came here to start trouble.
A crease cuts down between Roman's brows.
Too visible. Every lens will find you first.
The charcoal knit hangs easy on him; out of habit he shoves the sleeves to the forearm, baring thick wristbones and a ridge of vein.

en: The best seat I've ever had was the exit row on a red-eye. I was genuinely grateful for the extra four inches of legroom.
Roman sits across from him, knees nearly touching his. He opens a dark croc-grain leather case — the clasp gives a crisp click — and lays things out one at a time, steady as a man defusing a bomb.

en.title: The Inheritance Box
en.txt: Metal Black Card · Penthouse deed · Aviation credential · Board vote pass · Blue enamel family cufflink · Brass vault key

en: The case is lined in deep blue velvet, each item pressed into its own fitted slot, like everything was measured long ago and has just been waiting for him to claim it.
The aviation credential has his photo on it. Not an ID shot — a candid of him buying coffee on the corner, his jacket collar still folded under.
The black card is heavy, metal, cold at the edges. Almost nothing on it but a line of raised letters: ADRIAN VALE.
He drags his thumb over the unfamiliar surname, rough pad catching on each raised letter, like touching a scar on someone else's body.
For one second, holding it, I wanted it. Wanted it so bad my palm went hot. Then I remembered: nothing's free, and the expensive stuff least of all.
That's because you're thinking like someone who had thirty-two dollars yesterday.
The number attached to his name changed overnight. He didn't. He's still the guy who counts rent on his fingers at the end of the month.
Adrian picks up the brass key. Heavier than it looks, its teeth cut deep and dense. It warms fast in his big hand, giving off the sour tang of old metal.
Something your father refused to keep online.
Then the family cufflink: deep blue enamel set with a small silver crest. Roman's eyes catch on it. Barely. Adrian sees it anyway.
His gaze is still pinned to the cufflink. One forefinger taps the table edge once, then goes still.
Keep it. Don't give it to anyone.

en.title: Mystery: The Cufflink
en.txt: Vault key acquired. The blue cufflink stopped Roman's eyes for a full second. He won't explain.

t: roman
I've seen that cufflink once. Next to my father's old badge. Same deep blue, same crest. Not today.

en: The jet climbs into the clouds. The windows go wet white, then a blue so hard it hurts. Roman stands to stow the tablet in the overhead.
Then the floor drops out, the whole aircraft yanked down like a giant fist closed on the wing. Water leaps the rim of the glass and splashes across the walnut.
Adrian's feet go out; he grabs for a seat back, misses, and pitches forward. Roman has already turned — one hand clamped on his waist, the other locked on his forearm — and hauls him back by force.
Adrian slams into his chest, all six feet of him. Roman doesn't even sway.
The suit jacket falls open, and under the shirt the shape of shoulder and chest is suddenly very clear, hard as a wall. The hand at the small of his back is broad and hot and covers half his waist.
He breathes in Roman's collar: the cold fir bite of aftershave, and underneath it, the warmth of skin.
Roman's breathing doesn't change. Adrian's does, his chest heaving. He looks down at the hand still on his waist — hard knuckles, veins not yet sunk back under the skin.

en.hint: His hand is still on your waist, scalding through the shirt. Pressed this close, you can hear his heart — it's more honest than his face.
win: Roman's heart is at {bpm} — faster than Adrian's {mine}, slamming into the narrow space between their chests.
He looks down like he's only now noticed his hand. His fingers flex once. Half a second more, then he lets go.
lose: Roman's heart is at {bpm}, infuriatingly steady. But the hand still takes half a second too long, dragging a line of heat across Adrian's side as it goes.
skip: The hand takes half a second too long to let go. The heat of it stays on his waist after.

en.why: He didn't let go in the turbulence

en: Another jolt. Adrian throws out a hand for balance and his whole broad palm lands flat on Roman's chest. Through one thin layer of cotton, a heartbeat knocks, slow and heavy, against his hand.
Roman takes his wrist and doesn't push him away. His hand is bigger even than Adrian's; his thumb rests in Adrian's palm for half a second, a gun callus rasping across the lines.

en.hint: His hand is flat over your heart, palm burning, knuckles hard. Your heartbeat is giving you away.

opts.t: (very low) Do that again and I won't let go.
Roman doesn't let go. He presses Adrian's hand harder against his heart and holds it there two more seconds.
then: Two seconds is long enough for Adrian to count the beats — and to watch Roman's throat work around a swallow.

opts.t: Roman lets go at once and steps back. "Sit. Seatbelt."
then: Adrian sees it anyway: the skin behind Roman's ears, burning red.

en: The spilled water has soaked one of his cuffs. He shrugs off the jacket and drapes it over the seat back, thumbs open another shirt button, then rolls his sleeves to the elbow, turn by turn. His throat shifts in the loosened collar.
Without the jacket, the white shirt draws every line of him: wide shoulders, heavy chest, a waist that narrows hard. Below the rolled cuffs, his forearms flex with every move.
In the open collar, a length of the old scar under his collarbone shows, paler than the skin around it, like a sentence he never finished.
Adrian looks for one more second. Maybe two.
So I looked. He's the one who took the jacket off.

en.hint: Caught red-handed. Those grey eyes just wait for you — not looking away, not letting you off.

opts.t: I am looking up.
then: The skin behind Roman's ears goes faintly red. He turns his head, jawline cut sharp.
Only when the evidence is strong.
opts.rthink: I should button up. My hand gets as far as the collar and drops. Whatever he's looking at, it isn't the scar.

opts.t: Adrian whips his eyes to the clouds outside. Too fast. Guilty fast.
then: He goes back to swiping the tablet, holding down the faintest smile so it won't spread.
opts.rthink: That line got out on its own. Three years without a single slip, and he breaks me just by turning his head.

opts.t: Adrian lifts a hand and sets his fingertips on the scar under Roman's collarbone, through the shirt. "Checking for injuries."
then: The muscle under the cotton jumps hard. Roman clamps his wrist — doesn't push it away — thumb on his pulse, pressure tightening by degrees.
He lifts Adrian's hand off his chest, slowly, like he doesn't want to, his fingertips trailing the length of Adrian's knuckles.
opts.rthink: Nobody's touched this scar except the doctor who stitched it. One fingertip from him and I'm less steady than I was taking the blade.

opts.t: Ten years did a lot.
then: You said that when I was seventeen.
opts.rthink: He means the shoulders, not the man. Fine. If the man had changed, I wouldn't have taken this job three years ago.

en.title: The Turbulence That Almost Won
en.teaser: The third jolt, and the cabin lights stutter. In the dark his breath is right at your ear. Only the two of you know what happened in those three seconds.
then: The third drop comes out of nowhere. The lights snap off and on, and Adrian is thrown sideways, his shoulder slamming into the cold cabin panel.
Roman gets there first. One hand braced on the wall, forearm corded like steel cable, Adrian caged between him and the panel.
Close enough to count his lashes. Roman's breath grazes his ear, hot, with the bitter edge of black coffee.
Adrian doesn't. His hand has fisted in the front of Roman's shirt, knuckles digging into the cotton until it creases.
Roman bends his head. The tip of his nose drags down Adrian's, stubble scraping his cheekbone, and stops less than an inch above his mouth.
Do you know what I'm thinking.
Why I stopped, that night outside the store.
He rests his forehead against Adrian's and shuts his eyes. His breath stumbles. Then stumbles again.
Ding. The seatbelt sign lights up, a small amber glow falling between them.
Before he steps back, his thumb presses hard into Adrian's side, like a seal pressed into wax.
Next time there's no turbulence, I won't stop.

en: Forty-one thousand feet. The windows are packed with hard white glare; sunlight cuts across the cabin and lays a hot bar of gold over the walnut table.
The cream leather seats give off a sun-warmed smell, cut with the burnt bite of fresh coffee. The engines hum up through the cabin floor; ice ticks against glass.
They both agree, without a word, that the last few seconds never happened. Roman sits back down across from him. Adrian sits too. His breathing hasn't caught up.

Roman's suit jacket is still slung over the back of his seat. Shirtsleeves rolled to the elbow, veins running down his forearms; a plain steel watch on his left wrist, its band sitting over that pale old scar.
The clear earpiece is still in his left ear, its wire disappearing into his open collar, the scar under his collarbone showing at the edge. Those grey eyes are very deliberately not on Adrian.

Adrian is sunk in the seat opposite, all six feet of him filling the space between the armrests. The clothes he just changed into are pressed sharp, the shoulders fitted so close he keeps wanting to tug at them.
Great. Thirty seconds ago my hand was flat on his chest, and now I get to sit here admiring clouds. I write ad copy. I don't act.

A flight attendant comes back from the front cabin with two white cups on a tray. Before she's even close, Roman's eyes have done a full sweep: the door, the windows, the hand under her tray. Her face comes last.
Into any room: sweep the surroundings first, look at people second. He did it outside the building this morning. He did it ten years ago.
Mine black, no sugar. ...His with two sugars.
Adrian hasn't said a word. He takes the cup and sips. The sugar's already stirred in, exactly right.
Since when do you drink it like tar? You used to have mints in your pocket, always.
Quit sugar, quit people. Real discipline, these ten years.
Roman's jaw sets, the muscle hard under the stubble. That's what he does when he's rattled. He did it at eighteen.
The inheritance tablet on the table picks that moment to wake, throwing cold white light between them. One red line: HALFWAY POINT. SECONDARY IDENTITY CHECK REQUIRED BEFORE LANDING.
Memory check. Somebody got into your building's cameras this morning. After that, the trust doesn't fully believe fingerprints and faces.
It runs both ways. It asks me about you, then you about me. Proves you're you, and proves nobody swapped out your escort.
My files. Three years of them.
So my privacy left the building three years ago. Today's just the paperwork.
The first question slides up in a font so clean it's almost cruel: What does Adrian do when he's genuinely nervous?
(without looking up) Rubs his left wrist.
Adrian looks down. His right hand is already wrapped around his left wrist, a rough thumb working the knob of bone, slow and steady.
A habit he never noticed himself. Ten whole years, and Roman still knows it like he saw it yesterday.
Hell. He remembers that. So what else is he still carrying around?

en.hint: The check needs both of you. The tablet swivels, and its cold light lands on your face. Your turn to confirm the man across from you is really Roman.

qs.q: How does Roman take his coffee?
What does Roman do when he's rattled?
Roman walks into a room. What does he do first?
opts: Sweeps the room, then looks at people

qs.q: Ten years ago, what did Roman smell like?

win.title: MATCH {pct}%
win.txt: Four for four. Escort identity confirmed. Nobody memorizes another man down to the bone by accident.

win: A ring of green light runs around the tablet's edge. It flares in Roman's grey eyes and dies.
The rest is the years I wasn't there.
lose: The bar stalls on an in-between number, blinks twice, then prints a small line: MATCH {pct}%. VERIFIED. Roman glances at it and says nothing.
But the question about Adrian, he got dead right. He even knew which bone Adrian rubs when he's rattled.
skip: Roman reaches across the table and keys in an admin code. The questions vanish. One line is left: ESCORT IDENTITY CONFIRMED MANUALLY.

en.hint: Verified. The tablet goes quiet. The machine's done asking. You've got ten years of your own questions. Pick one, or don't.

opts.t: Ten years. What did you miss most?
then: Roman takes a long time. He looks out at all that white, jaw set in a hard clean line, before he finally speaks.
You yelling at me. Nobody else ever dared.
opts.rthink: That was my second answer. The first sits at the bottom of my camera roll—seventeen, laughing like nothing could touch him.

opts.t: Who looked away first that night?
then: Roman's jaw locks. A muscle rolls under the stubble. He doesn't argue.
opts.rthink: I looked away because one more second and I'd never have left the next morning. He doesn't know how close I came to staying.

opts.t: Adrian turns the tablet face down and asks nothing.
then: Roman looks at the face-down tablet. His shoulders drop half an inch, and something behind his eyes dims right along with them.
opts.rthink: He's done asking. I should be relieved. Three years I've had every answer ready, and he doesn't want a single one.

en: The tablet chimes and lights up again on its own. Verification cleared, a gold-foil animation floods up from the bottom of the screen: HEIR WELCOME BENEFIT / PERSONAL GIFT CREDIT.
The first item is a $40,000 watch, its platinum case glaring in the render. Yesterday he'd never have opened the page. Today it's suggested like a cup of coffee.
But a price tag has never moved Roman. Adrian just wants to see him pleased. The thought arrives so smoothly it's deeply inconvenient.
Get a grip, Adrian. He's on the clock. You're the job.

en.title: Gift Guess
en.hint: The most expensive isn't always right. Your finger hovers over the glass. How much of him do you still remember?

then: Roman unbuckles the old steel watch from his left wrist. Underneath, across the inside of the bone, the scar gone pale.
Adrian buckles the strap for him. His fingertip drags across the scar. Hot skin, and under it a pulse knocking against his finger.
You know I can do that myself.
Adrian presses the clasp home. Click. Only then does he look up.
I wanted to see if it looked good on you.
Roman looks at the faded cloth cover. His fingers stop on the cracked spine, knuckles going white.
He opens it. His name is still on the flyleaf in a seventeen-year-old's ballpoint, pressed so hard it tore the paper. He shuts it and is quiet a long time.
items.sub: The one he wore out at seventeen

then: You know how many sugars I take. We're even.
Roman slides the card into his inside pocket, the side over his heart, and flattens it there with his palm.
Roman lifts the cufflinks to the light; the engraving throws back a cold glint. He studies them a long time, but his eyes keep sliding to the Vale crest cufflink on the table.
Same maker. Where did you order these?
His jaw tightens. A vein rises at his temple.
I can't wear these on the job.
Then wear them off the job.
Roman holds the earbuds and blinks, like it has never once occurred to him that he has an 'off the job.'
items.sub: For a man who's always listening

items.t: That night's photo, printed and framed
then: Adrian skips the catalog and uploads the blurry old photo from his phone. Note: print it, walnut frame, deliver today.
The order confirmation pops up. The second Roman sees the thumbnail he goes completely still — seventeen-year-old Adrian on the step, eighteen-year-old him with a bandage on his lip.
His throat moves once. His fingers stay on the edge of the screen a long time, like he's holding something down.
So did you. The one in your album — same angle.
Roman doesn't deny it. He sets the tablet face-down on his knee and takes a long time to answer, low enough for only the two of them.
Not a new frame. Something old. Like it's been on a shelf ten years.

en: Roman reaches into the inside pocket of the jacket on his chair and comes out with an old keychain. He sets it in Adrian's palm. The brass is rubbed bright, edges worn round, still warm from his body.
Adrian closes his fist around it. The metal digs into the calluses on his palm, and that leftover warmth climbs straight up his forearm.

en.title: Memory: The Keychain He Never Threw Away
en.txt: Obviously a lie. Brass doesn't wear like that unless you've been holding it for years.

en: Adrian is about to ask how long, exactly, when the phone in his pocket buzzes. The moment the check cleared, the Vale family office synced its schedule to him.
The pinned item is edged in gold: "Per the late Mr. Alexander Vale's arrangements, your fiancée, Ms. Sienna Reed, will arrive at the penthouse at 6:00 PM tonight."
A work photo is attached. Chin-length dark-honey hair tucked behind one ear, pale green eyes, an ivory silk blouse under a camel coat.

A signet ring hangs on a thin chain at her throat instead of on her hand. She's in a conference-room doorway with a folder under her arm, and her smile for the camera is polite and brief, like she has another meeting after this one.
A father I never met lined up a fiancée I've never met. I haven't even figured out my own bank account yet.

He turns the phone toward Roman. Roman looks at the photo exactly once and doesn't scroll down, like he doesn't need to. Nothing moves in his face. Only the hand on the table's edge has stopped, knuckles gone white.

en.hint: A fiancée out of thin air. More interesting than the fiancée: Roman's frozen hand.

opts.t: Pretty?

then.hint: "Pretty?" He's doing it on purpose. You know he's watching how you answer.

opts.t: Irrelevant.
Wrong fit for you.
then: Adrian stares for a beat, then laughs, a low rough sound straight from the chest.
I said she lands at six.

opts.t: Roman reaches over and switches Adrian's screen off. "I'll find out what she's here for."
then: Checking her out, or guarding against her?

opts.rthink: He's watching how I answer. I've known Sienna Reed seven years. If she's coming, it isn't to marry anyone.

opts.t: If I get married, are you running security for that too?
then: Two seconds of silence. Nothing in the cabin but the low drone of the engines.
Everyone who walks through your door is my problem. Her included.
opts.rthink: Mine. Standing behind him while he puts a ring on someone else—I didn't price that in three years ago.

opts.t: Adrian doesn't ask anything. He just watches Roman's frozen hand.
then: Roman draws the hand back and closes it slowly into a fist. The veins on the back of it stand up one by one.
Look at that hand. His mouth won't give me a thing, but those veins are confessing everything.
Adrian doesn't push. He files the hand away.
opts.rthink: Not because of her. Because once she walks in, what happened seven years ago starts leaking out of her mouth.

en: The captain's voice comes from up front: landing security needs his sign-off. Roman stands, pulls his jacket off the chair and shrugs it on, takes two steps, and turns back.
You say that like I'm six.

en.txt: I saw her photo a long time ago. Didn't mention it. Didn't want to watch you nod early.

en: Unsent. Three seconds later, a new one: Don't touch anything till we land. It came from his work number. So whose number is the phone on the table?
On the corner of the table, Roman's black encrypted phone lights up. A thumbnail flashes past: Adrian at seventeen, grinning like nothing could ever touch him.
He shouldn't look. The other half of his brain says: he watched you behind your back for three years. 'Fair' is suddenly a very handy word.
Adrian's hand moves before his brain signs off. His big palm comes down over the phone, fingertips still holding the keychain's warmth.

en.hint: He's up front; his low voice leaks through the door. The screen's unlocked. You have maybe a minute.

items: He still doesn't know, does he?
How long are you going to keep this up?
If he comes home, you failed.

apps.lockTxt: Passcode required. Hint: the date of the convenience-store night.
items: Adrian and Roman at seventeen and eighteen, on the curb outside the store. Adrian hasn't learned the sharp smile yet. Roman hasn't learned to hide anything.
Saved ten years ago. Opened once a year since, on the same date.
I should have told him before today.
Unsent · 3 years ago / 1 year ago / yesterday
Wed 08:05 · Pick up A. Go yourself.
Directions · a convenience store in Brooklyn · 41 times

win: He sets the phone back exactly where it was, same angle, even the window glare lined up on the glass.
He kept that photo. For ten years.
The draft is worse than the photo. It means he thought about coming back. He just didn't, again and again.
lose: Adrian looks once and turns the phone face down, palms gone damp. His heartbeat is louder than the snooping.
But the thumbnail of his seventeen-year-old face is already burned in.
skip: Adrian pushes the phone back without touching the glass. Some things he wants to hear out of Roman's own mouth.

en: The cabin door slides open and Roman comes back with a draft of cold air and a trace of cedar aftershave. The phone's at the same angle. The brightness isn't.
His grey eyes rest on the phone for half a second, then move to Adrian's face. He says nothing. That half second lasts as long as an interrogation.

en.hint: He's been through your phone. He put it back carefully, angle perfect. Carefully enough to look guilty.

opts.t: Roman holds his eyes for a second, swallows, and asks nothing.
Enjoy my phone?
then: Adrian doesn't blink. His chin lifts a fraction, a grin held down under the stubble.
You should really lock your screen.
Roman stares at him for two seconds, lets out a short breath through his nose, and drops it.

opts.t: Roman picks up the phone and sets a passcode right in front of him.
then: Four digits, punched in slow, like he wants them seen. Adrian knows them. The date of the convenience-store night.

en: Adrian opens his mouth, and the black phone lights up again. Unknown number. Voice message, 00:06. A red dot pulses in the corner.

en.title: Voice Message · Unknown Number
en.txt: A voice scraped raw by distortion, nothing human left in it: "Cross, walk away."

en: Something in Roman switches over. Spine straight, eyes gone flat. Not fear. A hound catching blood on the wind.
One swipe of his thumb and the message is dead. The veins stand out across the back of his hand, knuckles pinning the screen, so fast it almost cuts the air.
Fast enough that it's about Adrian not hearing. People hide things for two reasons: it could hurt them, or it could hurt you.
Cross — Roman's surname. Everyone he grew up with called him Roman. Only someone handling him like a codename would use the surname alone.
(Cross is Roman's surname. In his line of work, first names are for friends; surnames are for files and call signs.)

en.hint: He killed it. You didn't even catch whether the voice was a man's or a woman's.

opts.t: Play it again.
opts.rthink: Play it again and he'll ask who Cross is. Seven years are buried under that name. I haven't decided where to start digging.
