then: Adrian saw the hand stop. He saw it shake.

es: Ten years, and that's what you open with?
Adrian walks right up to him, boots grinding through a puddle. Not much shorter. Chin up, the muscle in his jaw a hard ridge under the stubble.
Close enough to smell him: cedar, gun oil, a trace of cold smoke. Ten years ago he only ever smelled like spearmint.
He doesn't argue. He opens the back door himself and braces one hand on the frame above it — a stance that could be shielding a man, or cutting off his exit.

es.hint: You rehearsed this for forty minutes in the car until your palms were wet. There's no right way to say it.

opts.t: Your father died yesterday.
Adrian, let me finish. ...Your father died yesterday.
then: He says it slowly, word by word, gray eyes never leaving Adrian's face, like he's waiting for the swing.

opts.t: Roman doesn't say it. He hands over the tablet, the obituary on screen.
then: White on black, cold as a headstone. Adrian reads the headline: ALEXANDER VALE DIES AT 61.

es: For the first time, the sarcasm drains off Adrian's face — like someone yanked away the shield he's held up his whole life.
The street noise pulls away. All he hears is his own heartbeat, slow and heavy, like someone dragging an iron trunk across the floor upstairs.
You do. His name was Alexander Vale.

es.title: Your Father Was Alexander Vale
es.txt: Hotels, banks, airlines, media — half the names on the Manhattan skyline. That Vale.

es: The door shuts with a click like a safe locking. The building, the store, the bus stop slide away behind dark soundproof glass.
The cabin smells of new leather and cold air, so quiet he can hear the vents breathe. His worn-out jeans on cream leather look like a burglar who wandered in.
Roman sits beside him, suit trousers pulled tight over heavy thighs, his knee a fist's width away. Every turn sways his body heat across the gap.
Roman takes a black leather folder from the front seat and sets it on Adrian's knees. His hand stays on Adrian's knee a fraction of a second too long.
Black calfskin, heavier than his old laptop. No words on the cover, just a silver V pressed into the bottom corner, the edges rubbed shiny. Somebody has opened this a lot.
Inside, heavy paper, a watermark showing against the window. Page one: ALEXANDER VALE — DECEASED. Page two: PATERNITY CONFIRMATION. Page three: ADRIAN HALE / 99.998% MATCH.
He skips the assets and reads the DNA result twice, thumb pressed down on the number so hard the nail goes white.
The number is too precise to hide behind 'there's been a mistake.'
No thunder. No soundtrack. His life just got rewritten on one expensive sheet of paper, in a car that is far too quiet.
Twenty-seven years, not one photo. Now he's dead, and suddenly he remembers to drop a paternity test in my lap.
He died yesterday. And today I'm suddenly his son?
You were his son yesterday too.
Roman gives him a few seconds — watches his throat work twice — before he unlocks the tablet: VALE GROUP — CONTROLLING BENEFICIAL HEIR.
At the top of the screen, a card. Matte black, a hairline of gold around the edge, and dead center a number field under a frosted seal. All he can tell is that the number is long.

Below it, a column of logos, one after another: the bank he passes on the train every morning, the hotel by his office he has never once walked into, the row of white tail fins with a V on them at the end of the runway.
He notices his thumb is already resting on the seal. He takes it back and wipes it on his jeans.
Five years writing ads, and I've typed "life-changing" a hundred times. Turns out the real thing looks like this: a box you can't open.
Enough that the number stops helping. Controlling interests. Private aviation. Hotels. Media. Real estate. Banking.
This morning I had thirty-two dollars and eighteen cents.
The bank holding that thirty-two dollars? You own part of it now.

es.hint: A number you haven't even read yet is sitting on your knees, heavy as hot iron. Your first move is—

opts.t: Give me the complete list. No summaries.
then: Adrian pulls the tablet back toward himself and starts swiping fast.
I just prefer being shocked with information.
Roman's mouth twitches, like a fish moving under ice. The screen unfolds: Black Card. Manhattan penthouse. Private aviation. Temporary board vote.
opts.rthink: He wants the full list, not the summary. Good. As long as he doesn't ask who compiled it—I've had it memorized for three years.

opts.t: Did my mother know?
then: For the first time, Roman looks careful. The muscle in his jaw shifts, like he's grinding a sentence he isn't allowed to say.
It's the answer I can give you right now.
She spent her whole life counting bills.
Adrian's fingers press down on the asset page, knuckles standing out, creasing the paper.
Your mother made choices to keep you away from this family.

then.title: Clue: She Knew More
then.txt: For three whole seconds the money stops feeling like a prize — and starts feeling like a door your mother held shut for twenty-seven years.

opts.rthink: She knew more than I'm allowed to say. One more question and I'd have to choose: lie to him, or make him hate her.

opts.t: Adrian jabs his thumb down and kills the asset page.
then: You don't want to see it?
I want to know why you're the one showing it to me. How long?
Roman pauses. Window light strobes across his face, one bar at a time, and never reaches his eyes.
Three years. It hits harder than any number on that page. Money explains the cars. It doesn't explain three years of watching and never once walking over.
opts.rthink: Four point eight billion, killed with one thumb. He never looks at the money first. He looks at the person. I'd rather he looked at the money.

opts.t: Stop the car. I'm verifying this myself.
then: Someone accessed your building cameras at 6:14 this morning.
He slides his encrypted phone across. The black case is still warm from his palm.
Verify the DNA. Verify me. Verify the lawyers. But do it while moving.
Lab receipt. The official Vale obituary. Roman's security clearance. The law-firm filing. Adrian checks every one, his thumb slowing with each. All real.
opts.rthink: Stop? After 6:14 I can't vouch for a single window on this street. If he gets out, I'll haul him back in and take the punch.

es: Roman taps the corner of the tablet with a callused forefinger. The asset page shrinks away. Four black-and-white feeds take its place, snow hissing at the edges.
The part nobody puts in the inheritance brochure. Someone got into your building's cameras at 6:14 this morning. These are the four feeds from that minute.
Most likely. The other possibility is worse.
The air in the car seems to drop two degrees. The hair on the back of Adrian's neck stands up.
This is the moment the inheritance stops being absurd and starts being dangerous.
Four feeds, one timecode: 06:14. Adrian goes through them one at a time.
CAM A, stairwell: an old woman in a bathrobe working her way down, one hand on the rail. Mrs. Ortiz, 3B, going for her paper.
CAM B, front stoop: a delivery guy drops two bags on the step, yawns straight into the lens, and leaves.
CAM C, back door: a man in a work jacket with a toolbox comes up the alley — the radiator guy, by the look of him. He takes the handle, pulls, and the door swings open. He steps inside.
CAM D, lobby: Hector the super, mop and bucket, working the floor.
Nothing, at first glance. One beat-up building, one morning, four completely ordinary people.

es.hint: Roman turns the tablet toward you. "You've lived in that building three years. You'll see what's wrong faster than I will."

es.hint2: Clues: Mrs. Ortiz goes down for her paper at 6:15 every day; last week Hector chained the back door shut from the inside. One of these four things cannot happen in that building — tap it.

cams.clue: Mrs. Ortiz heading down for her paper around 6:15 — same as every day for three years.
The delivery guy yawns right into the lens, drops the bags, leaves.
Hector chained the back door from the inside last week. This man pulls it open from the outside — and never shows the camera his face, every step in a blind spot.
Hector mopping the lobby. Business as usual.

win: The back door. Hector chained it from the inside last week. You can't open it from the alley.
Roman turns his head and looks at him — a long look, like confirming something he already knew.
He knows. How the hell does he know what's on our back door?

win.txt: A chained door that opens for him. Every blind spot, avoided. Whoever this is knows Vale's security system.

win: I let that one go. Pick it up and I'd have to ask why. Ask why, and I'd have to hear the answer.

Back door's been chained from the inside since last week. Can't be opened from the alley. He just pulled it open.
...How does he know about the chain on our back door?
On screen, the man never once faces the camera. Every step lands in a blind spot.

t: roman
I flagged that blind spot three years ago. Nobody fixed it. Today somebody used it. Whoever he is — he touches one hair on Adrian's head, and I'll teach him personally what a blind spot is.

es.place: Vale motorcade, en route to the airfield

es: The SUV's windows are tinted so dark the September sun comes through cold and blue-grey. The cabin smells of new leather and cedar, too clean for anyone to have ever lived in it.

Adrian has the window side of the back seat, six feet of him folded into leather built for men who sit still. Army-green jacket washed thin, the grey T-shirt under it stretched out at the collar, work boots splitting at the toe.
He hasn't slept. Stubble has come in dark along his jaw, shadows dug in under his eyes. One big hand rests on his knee, knuckles still pale from gripping something too long.

Roman sits beside him, spine straight as a rifle barrel. Black suit cut close to the body, shoulders broad and squared, white collar points razor-crisp, a clear earpiece in his left ear, its coil vanishing under the collar.
Dark hair clipped close to the skull. Grey eyes fixed on the road, quietly counting every car that slides past. A steel watch on his wrist, and under the band, a pale old scar.
Ten years, and the man sits like a knife in a sheath. Me: a stretched-out T-shirt, two days of stubble, and boots with their mouths hanging open.

then: Three years. The number follows him like a nail in a tire, out of the Brooklyn brownstones and onto a highway still slick with morning fog.
Roman's profile hangs in the tinted glass, perfectly still. Not even the line of his jaw gives.
else: Cup holder. That one's yours. Two sugars.
Adrian looks down. Still hot. Two sugars, no cream. He never said a word about it. If Roman only took this job today, how does he know?
How long have you known about me?

else.hint: He asked. His eyes are nailed to your face, jaw locked, and the only sound is tires hissing on asphalt. You can lie, you can stall, or you can tell him.

opts.t: (half a second of silence) Three years.
...Long enough.
Roman doesn't answer. One swipe of his thumb, and the tablet's cold light catches his knuckles: ASSIGNMENT START DATE. Three years ago today.
then: Adrian stares at the date. His Adam's apple works once. He doesn't say anything for a long time.

es: Three years means Roman knows about the move from Queens to the Brooklyn attic with the leaking skylight. The three jobs. The weekends moonlighting for a moving company, hauling refrigerators up five flights to make rent.
Knows that last winter two guys boxed him in behind a bar, and he took one punch and gave back three, then went home and put six stitches in the back of his own hand in the bathroom mirror.
Knows he rolled an ankle in a pickup game, played out the last round anyway, limped twenty blocks home, and clocked in the next morning like nothing happened.
Being walked out on was simple: you hate the guy, then you slowly forget him. Finding out he was a street away the whole time, watching through a windshield, is harder to swallow.
That night in the alley it was two on one, and I bought the needle and thread at the bodega downstairs. If he was across the street watching, I hope he got a good look: I never once yelled for help.
That night in the alley. Were you 'protecting' me then?
Across the street. By the time I stepped off the curb, you didn't need me.
So you stood there and watched.
Your right hook's heavier than it was at seventeen.
Adrian's jaw locks. Somehow the compliment lands harder than the punch did.

es.hint: Three years across the street — watching you haul freight, take hits, hit back — and he never once crossed over. How do you handle it?

opts.t: Fine. I'll take half of it on faith.
then: Half is more than I've earned.
Roman looks at him for a long time. Something in those grey eyes sinks, then slowly surfaces again.
opts.rthink: Half. Ten years ago he handed me all of it and I dropped it. I'll earn back the rest if it kills me.

opts.t: A good suit doesn't turn stalking into protection.
then: Roman glances down at the knife-pressed front of his suit, then back up, one eyebrow lifting a fraction.
The second half was the point.
opts.rthink: He said the suit looks good. I'll keep that. The rest he's right about—I called myself the same thing that night in the alley.

opts.t: Was it my father?
then: Roman's pupils tighten; a muscle jumps along his jaw. Fast. Adrian catches it anyway.
That was me regretting eye contact.

then.title: Clue: Father May Have Hired Roman
then.txt: Alexander Vale found him three years before he died — earlier than any will.

opts.rthink: Old Vale had one condition three years ago: never let him know who was paying. I just breached it with half a look.

opts.t: So where I drink on Friday nights, and till when — that's in the report too?
then: Roman turns to the window. His throat moves above the starched collar.
The place on Seventh. Third stool from the left. Usually till one-forty.
Adrian laughs — low, rough from no sleep, the sound coming up from deep in his chest.
The bartender comped you three times. Irregular transactions. I log those.
We're coming off the highway. Sit back.
But the hand on his knee has closed into a fist, veins rising one by one across the back of it, his jaw set like he's grinding something to dust.
Irregular transactions. Three free beers from a bartender, and he filed them as irregular transactions. Noted. So the man does have a pressure point.
opts.rthink: The third free round, the bartender put a hand on his shoulder. I rewrote that report four times. All that survived was 'billing irregularity.'

es: Outside, the brick walk-ups and coin laundries fall away, replaced by grey airport service roads, chain-link fence, and rows of blank-faced freight warehouses.
Ten years ago, Roman was right beside him. Then seven years of nothing. Then three years of 'protection' — without ever once showing his face.
Those seven years were cut out of the timeline with a blade. Clean edges. Not one loose thread.
Roman's fingers slowly close on his knee, knuckles rising one by one, crushing creases into the wool.
Roman finally turns his head. Those grey eyes come straight at him, close enough to see what's being held down in them.
A summer night ten years ago, the rain thick and airless. The convenience store's AC unit rattling on the wall, fluorescent tubes buzzing overhead, puddles holding their sick white light.
Eighteen-year-old Roman sat on the floor against the ice chest, lip split, the blood dried dark. His knuckles were skinned raw, the collar of his T-shirt yanked crooked.
Adrian tore the bandage open with his teeth, hands not quite steady. As he pressed it on, they kept leaning closer, close enough to smell rain and rust and mint candy on him.
Roman's thumb brushed behind Adrian's ear, rough and burning. Half an inch between their mouths.
The AC unit kept humming. Rain drummed on the awning. Neither of them moved.
One blink and it's twenty-eight-year-old Roman, less than an arm's length away. Shoulders a full size wider than they were, a frame that fills the suit without a wasted inch.
His voice has dropped into his chest. His collar lifts and settles with each breath, and under the stiff points, the tail end of an old scar shows just below his collarbone.
At seventeen, wanting to kiss him was confusing. At twenty-seven, the problem is clarity — wanting it so precisely his back teeth ache.
Cool it. He's your bodyguard. You pay his salary. Fine — your dead father does.

es.hint: That half inch has been hanging between you for ten years. The only sound is the low breath of the vents. This time — do you move?

opts.t: Adrian reaches over and runs a rough fingertip along the pale scar on his wrist.
then: Roman catches his wrist on instinct — fast as a draw, but gentle, his thumb landing square on Adrian's hammering pulse.
The heat of that palm stays on Adrian's wristbone half a second too long before he lets go.
opts.rthink: This one's nothing. The one that hurts is under my collarbone—I got it the year I left. One more question and I'd have told him everything.

opts.t: The car banks into a turn. Adrian's knee settles against his thigh and stays there.
then: Through the thin suit wool, the muscle in Roman's thigh turns to iron. He looks down, lashes low.
Roman leans back into the leather as if to put distance between them. His knee doesn't move an inch.
That's an answer. Adrian turns to the window so he won't grin.
opts.rthink: I should move. Every muscle in my leg is waiting for the order. I don't give it. I've started counting the turns left on this road.

opts.t: Adrian says nothing. He just watches Roman's mouth.
then: Roman's words slow down. His Adam's apple drags once above that stiff collar.
That's usually when you're most dangerous.
opts.rthink: He's watching my mouth exactly like that night. I stopped then, and I was gone by morning. He still thinks those are two separate things.

opts.t: Later. Inheritance first.
then: Maybe ten years taught me boundaries.
Roman huffs a quiet laugh through his nose.
opts.rthink: He stopped. I should be relieved. But the kid who never hit the brakes at seventeen—I'm the one who taught him how.

es.title: VALE ONE
lines: Before he sees the plane, he hears it: the last hangar's doors rolling apart on rumbling steel tracks, an idling engine's drone climbing up through his boot soles.
The gap widens. First a wing, long and thin, its tip curled up like the spine of a blade; then the whole fuselage, pure white, one deep-blue pinstripe from nose to tail.
High on the tail fin, four silver letters: VALE. Each one taller than he is. A deep red runner is laid from the airstair to the car door and stops exactly there.
His split-toed boots land on the red. At the foot of the stairs a line of navy uniforms bows as one: "Good morning, Mr. Vale." The first time anyone has said that name to his face.
The door seals behind him with a heavy thunk and the engine roar drops to a distant hum. Thick wool carpet swallows his footsteps whole.
Pale grey suede walls, walnut polished enough to show him his own stubble. Cream lambskin seats, the armrests stitched in the same deep blue as the stripe outside.
At the back, a sliding door stands half open on a made-up bed and a marble bathroom. His whole leaking attic would fit in here and still leave room for an aisle.
Yesterday he missed a train and nobody on the platform looked up. Today a jet sits burning fuel for the three minutes he was late. He stands in the aisle and doesn't sit down.

es: Last month I walked forty minutes to a client to save the two-ninety subway fare. Now a jet is idling just for me, burning fuel by the gallon. Nobody burns that for free. The bill's coming.
That's probably why they chose you.

es.title: Styling
es.hint: An assistant wheels a rolling rack down the aisle, three looks hanging razor-straight, garment bags still warm from the steamer. There'll be cameras at the foot of the stairs when they land.

then: The black wool drops clean off his shoulders and tapers hard at the waist; suddenly even the stubble on his jaw looks deliberate.
Roman's gaze travels from the sharp collar across the breadth of his shoulders and down to the inch of wrist at the cuff. It stops there for a second.
The cream suit glows in the cold light from the windows, and against it his sun-dark throat and rough stubble make him look like a man who came here to start trouble.
A crease cuts down between Roman's brows.
Too visible. Every lens will find you first.
The charcoal knit hangs easy on him; out of habit he shoves the sleeves to the forearm, baring thick wristbones and a ridge of vein.

es: The best seat I've ever had was the exit row on a red-eye. I was genuinely grateful for the extra four inches of legroom.
Roman sits across from him, knees nearly touching his. He opens a dark croc-grain leather case — the clasp gives a crisp click — and lays things out one at a time, steady as a man defusing a bomb.

es.title: The Inheritance Box
es.txt: Metal Black Card · Penthouse deed · Aviation credential · Board vote pass · Blue enamel family cufflink · Brass vault key

es: The case is lined in deep blue velvet, each item pressed into its own fitted slot, like everything was measured long ago and has just been waiting for him to claim it.
The aviation credential has his photo on it. Not an ID shot — a candid of him buying coffee on the corner, his jacket collar still folded under.
The black card is heavy, metal, cold at the edges. Almost nothing on it but a line of raised letters: ADRIAN VALE.
He drags his thumb over the unfamiliar surname, rough pad catching on each raised letter, like touching a scar on someone else's body.
For one second, holding it, I wanted it. Wanted it so bad my palm went hot. Then I remembered: nothing's free, and the expensive stuff least of all.
That's because you're thinking like someone who had thirty-two dollars yesterday.
The number attached to his name changed overnight. He didn't. He's still the guy who counts rent on his fingers at the end of the month.
Adrian picks up the brass key. Heavier than it looks, its teeth cut deep and dense. It warms fast in his big hand, giving off the sour tang of old metal.
Something your father refused to keep online.
Then the family cufflink: deep blue enamel set with a small silver crest. Roman's eyes catch on it. Barely. Adrian sees it anyway.
His gaze is still pinned to the cufflink. One forefinger taps the table edge once, then goes still.
Keep it. Don't give it to anyone.

es.title: Mystery: The Cufflink
es.txt: Vault key acquired. The blue cufflink stopped Roman's eyes for a full second. He won't explain.

t: roman
I've seen that cufflink once. Next to my father's old badge. Same deep blue, same crest. Not today.

es: The jet climbs into the clouds. The windows go wet white, then a blue so hard it hurts. Roman stands to stow the tablet in the overhead.
Then the floor drops out, the whole aircraft yanked down like a giant fist closed on the wing. Water leaps the rim of the glass and splashes across the walnut.
Adrian's feet go out; he grabs for a seat back, misses, and pitches forward. Roman has already turned — one hand clamped on his waist, the other locked on his forearm — and hauls him back by force.
Adrian slams into his chest, all six feet of him. Roman doesn't even sway.
The suit jacket falls open, and under the shirt the shape of shoulder and chest is suddenly very clear, hard as a wall. The hand at the small of his back is broad and hot and covers half his waist.
He breathes in Roman's collar: the cold fir bite of aftershave, and underneath it, the warmth of skin.
Roman's breathing doesn't change. Adrian's does, his chest heaving. He looks down at the hand still on his waist — hard knuckles, veins not yet sunk back under the skin.

es.hint: His hand is still on your waist, scalding through the shirt. Pressed this close, you can hear his heart — it's more honest than his face.
win: Roman's heart is at {bpm} — faster than Adrian's {mine}, slamming into the narrow space between their chests.
He looks down like he's only now noticed his hand. His fingers flex once. Half a second more, then he lets go.
lose: Roman's heart is at {bpm}, infuriatingly steady. But the hand still takes half a second too long, dragging a line of heat across Adrian's side as it goes.
skip: The hand takes half a second too long to let go. The heat of it stays on his waist after.

es.why: He didn't let go in the turbulence

es: Another jolt. Adrian throws out a hand for balance and his whole broad palm lands flat on Roman's chest. Through one thin layer of cotton, a heartbeat knocks, slow and heavy, against his hand.
Roman takes his wrist and doesn't push him away. His hand is bigger even than Adrian's; his thumb rests in Adrian's palm for half a second, a gun callus rasping across the lines.

es.hint: His hand is flat over your heart, palm burning, knuckles hard. Your heartbeat is giving you away.

opts.t: (very low) Do that again and I won't let go.
Roman doesn't let go. He presses Adrian's hand harder against his heart and holds it there two more seconds.
then: Two seconds is long enough for Adrian to count the beats — and to watch Roman's throat work around a swallow.

opts.t: Roman lets go at once and steps back. "Sit. Seatbelt."
then: Adrian sees it anyway: the skin behind Roman's ears, burning red.

es: The spilled water has soaked one of his cuffs. He shrugs off the jacket and drapes it over the seat back, thumbs open another shirt button, then rolls his sleeves to the elbow, turn by turn. His throat shifts in the loosened collar.
Without the jacket, the white shirt draws every line of him: wide shoulders, heavy chest, a waist that narrows hard. Below the rolled cuffs, his forearms flex with every move.
In the open collar, a length of the old scar under his collarbone shows, paler than the skin around it, like a sentence he never finished.
Adrian looks for one more second. Maybe two.
So I looked. He's the one who took the jacket off.

es.hint: Caught red-handed. Those grey eyes just wait for you — not looking away, not letting you off.

opts.t: I am looking up.
then: The skin behind Roman's ears goes faintly red. He turns his head, jawline cut sharp.
Only when the evidence is strong.
opts.rthink: I should button up. My hand gets as far as the collar and drops. Whatever he's looking at, it isn't the scar.

opts.t: Adrian whips his eyes to the clouds outside. Too fast. Guilty fast.
then: He goes back to swiping the tablet, holding down the faintest smile so it won't spread.
opts.rthink: That line got out on its own. Three years without a single slip, and he breaks me just by turning his head.

opts.t: Adrian lifts a hand and sets his fingertips on the scar under Roman's collarbone, through the shirt. "Checking for injuries."
then: The muscle under the cotton jumps hard. Roman clamps his wrist — doesn't push it away — thumb on his pulse, pressure tightening by degrees.
He lifts Adrian's hand off his chest, slowly, like he doesn't want to, his fingertips trailing the length of Adrian's knuckles.
opts.rthink: Nobody's touched this scar except the doctor who stitched it. One fingertip from him and I'm less steady than I was taking the blade.

opts.t: Ten years did a lot.
then: You said that when I was seventeen.
opts.rthink: He means the shoulders, not the man. Fine. If the man had changed, I wouldn't have taken this job three years ago.

es.title: The Turbulence That Almost Won
es.teaser: The third jolt, and the cabin lights stutter. In the dark his breath is right at your ear. Only the two of you know what happened in those three seconds.
then: The third drop comes out of nowhere. The lights snap off and on, and Adrian is thrown sideways, his shoulder slamming into the cold cabin panel.
Roman gets there first. One hand braced on the wall, forearm corded like steel cable, Adrian caged between him and the panel.
Close enough to count his lashes. Roman's breath grazes his ear, hot, with the bitter edge of black coffee.
Adrian doesn't. His hand has fisted in the front of Roman's shirt, knuckles digging into the cotton until it creases.
Roman bends his head. The tip of his nose drags down Adrian's, stubble scraping his cheekbone, and stops less than an inch above his mouth.
Do you know what I'm thinking.
Why I stopped, that night outside the store.
He rests his forehead against Adrian's and shuts his eyes. His breath stumbles. Then stumbles again.
Ding. The seatbelt sign lights up, a small amber glow falling between them.
Before he steps back, his thumb presses hard into Adrian's side, like a seal pressed into wax.
Next time there's no turbulence, I won't stop.

es: Forty-one thousand feet. The windows are packed with hard white glare; sunlight cuts across the cabin and lays a hot bar of gold over the walnut table.
The cream leather seats give off a sun-warmed smell, cut with the burnt bite of fresh coffee. The engines hum up through the cabin floor; ice ticks against glass.
They both agree, without a word, that the last few seconds never happened. Roman sits back down across from him. Adrian sits too. His breathing hasn't caught up.

Roman's suit jacket is still slung over the back of his seat. Shirtsleeves rolled to the elbow, veins running down his forearms; a plain steel watch on his left wrist, its band sitting over that pale old scar.
The clear earpiece is still in his left ear, its wire disappearing into his open collar, the scar under his collarbone showing at the edge. Those grey eyes are very deliberately not on Adrian.

Adrian is sunk in the seat opposite, all six feet of him filling the space between the armrests. The clothes he just changed into are pressed sharp, the shoulders fitted so close he keeps wanting to tug at them.
Great. Thirty seconds ago my hand was flat on his chest, and now I get to sit here admiring clouds. I write ad copy. I don't act.

A flight attendant comes back from the front cabin with two white cups on a tray. Before she's even close, Roman's eyes have done a full sweep: the door, the windows, the hand under her tray. Her face comes last.
Into any room: sweep the surroundings first, look at people second. He did it outside the building this morning. He did it ten years ago.
Mine black, no sugar. ...His with two sugars.
Adrian hasn't said a word. He takes the cup and sips. The sugar's already stirred in, exactly right.
Since when do you drink it like tar? You used to have mints in your pocket, always.
Quit sugar, quit people. Real discipline, these ten years.
Roman's jaw sets, the muscle hard under the stubble. That's what he does when he's rattled. He did it at eighteen.
The inheritance tablet on the table picks that moment to wake, throwing cold white light between them. One red line: HALFWAY POINT. SECONDARY IDENTITY CHECK REQUIRED BEFORE LANDING.
Memory check. Somebody got into your building's cameras this morning. After that, the trust doesn't fully believe fingerprints and faces.
It runs both ways. It asks me about you, then you about me. Proves you're you, and proves nobody swapped out your escort.
My files. Three years of them.
So my privacy left the building three years ago. Today's just the paperwork.
The first question slides up in a font so clean it's almost cruel: What does Adrian do when he's genuinely nervous?
(without looking up) Rubs his left wrist.
Adrian looks down. His right hand is already wrapped around his left wrist, a rough thumb working the knob of bone, slow and steady.
A habit he never noticed himself. Ten whole years, and Roman still knows it like he saw it yesterday.
Hell. He remembers that. So what else is he still carrying around?

es.hint: The check needs both of you. The tablet swivels, and its cold light lands on your face. Your turn to confirm the man across from you is really Roman.

qs.q: How does Roman take his coffee?
What does Roman do when he's rattled?
Roman walks into a room. What does he do first?
opts: Sweeps the room, then looks at people

qs.q: Ten years ago, what did Roman smell like?

win.title: MATCH {pct}%
win.txt: Four for four. Escort identity confirmed. Nobody memorizes another man down to the bone by accident.

win: A ring of green light runs around the tablet's edge. It flares in Roman's grey eyes and dies.
The rest is the years I wasn't there.
lose: The bar stalls on an in-between number, blinks twice, then prints a small line: MATCH {pct}%. VERIFIED. Roman glances at it and says nothing.
But the question about Adrian, he got dead right. He even knew which bone Adrian rubs when he's rattled.
skip: Roman reaches across the table and keys in an admin code. The questions vanish. One line is left: ESCORT IDENTITY CONFIRMED MANUALLY.

es.hint: Verified. The tablet goes quiet. The machine's done asking. You've got ten years of your own questions. Pick one, or don't.

opts.t: Ten years. What did you miss most?
then: Roman takes a long time. He looks out at all that white, jaw set in a hard clean line, before he finally speaks.
You yelling at me. Nobody else ever dared.
opts.rthink: That was my second answer. The first sits at the bottom of my camera roll—seventeen, laughing like nothing could touch him.

opts.t: Who looked away first that night?
then: Roman's jaw locks. A muscle rolls under the stubble. He doesn't argue.
opts.rthink: I looked away because one more second and I'd never have left the next morning. He doesn't know how close I came to staying.

opts.t: Adrian turns the tablet face down and asks nothing.
then: Roman looks at the face-down tablet. His shoulders drop half an inch, and something behind his eyes dims right along with them.
opts.rthink: He's done asking. I should be relieved. Three years I've had every answer ready, and he doesn't want a single one.

es: The tablet chimes and lights up again on its own. Verification cleared, a gold-foil animation floods up from the bottom of the screen: HEIR WELCOME BENEFIT / PERSONAL GIFT CREDIT.
The first item is a $40,000 watch, its platinum case glaring in the render. Yesterday he'd never have opened the page. Today it's suggested like a cup of coffee.
But a price tag has never moved Roman. Adrian just wants to see him pleased. The thought arrives so smoothly it's deeply inconvenient.
Get a grip, Adrian. He's on the clock. You're the job.

es.title: Gift Guess
es.hint: The most expensive isn't always right. Your finger hovers over the glass. How much of him do you still remember?

then: Roman unbuckles the old steel watch from his left wrist. Underneath, across the inside of the bone, the scar gone pale.
Adrian buckles the strap for him. His fingertip drags across the scar. Hot skin, and under it a pulse knocking against his finger.
You know I can do that myself.
Adrian presses the clasp home. Click. Only then does he look up.
I wanted to see if it looked good on you.
Roman looks at the faded cloth cover. His fingers stop on the cracked spine, knuckles going white.
He opens it. His name is still on the flyleaf in a seventeen-year-old's ballpoint, pressed so hard it tore the paper. He shuts it and is quiet a long time.
items.sub: The one he wore out at seventeen

then: You know how many sugars I take. We're even.
Roman slides the card into his inside pocket, the side over his heart, and flattens it there with his palm.
Roman lifts the cufflinks to the light; the engraving throws back a cold glint. He studies them a long time, but his eyes keep sliding to the Vale crest cufflink on the table.
Same maker. Where did you order these?
His jaw tightens. A vein rises at his temple.
I can't wear these on the job.
Then wear them off the job.
Roman holds the earbuds and blinks, like it has never once occurred to him that he has an 'off the job.'
items.sub: For a man who's always listening

items.t: That night's photo, printed and framed
then: Adrian skips the catalog and uploads the blurry old photo from his phone. Note: print it, walnut frame, deliver today.
The order confirmation pops up. The second Roman sees the thumbnail he goes completely still — seventeen-year-old Adrian on the step, eighteen-year-old him with a bandage on his lip.
His throat moves once. His fingers stay on the edge of the screen a long time, like he's holding something down.
So did you. The one in your album — same angle.
Roman doesn't deny it. He sets the tablet face-down on his knee and takes a long time to answer, low enough for only the two of them.
Not a new frame. Something old. Like it's been on a shelf ten years.

es: Roman reaches into the inside pocket of the jacket on his chair and comes out with an old keychain. He sets it in Adrian's palm. The brass is rubbed bright, edges worn round, still warm from his body.
Adrian closes his fist around it. The metal digs into the calluses on his palm, and that leftover warmth climbs straight up his forearm.

es.title: Memory: The Keychain He Never Threw Away
es.txt: Obviously a lie. Brass doesn't wear like that unless you've been holding it for years.

es: Adrian is about to ask how long, exactly, when the phone in his pocket buzzes. The moment the check cleared, the Vale family office synced its schedule to him.
The pinned item is edged in gold: "Per the late Mr. Alexander Vale's arrangements, your fiancée, Ms. Sienna Reed, will arrive at the penthouse at 6:00 PM tonight."
A work photo is attached. Chin-length dark-honey hair tucked behind one ear, pale green eyes, an ivory silk blouse under a camel coat.

A signet ring hangs on a thin chain at her throat instead of on her hand. She's in a conference-room doorway with a folder under her arm, and her smile for the camera is polite and brief, like she has another meeting after this one.
A father I never met lined up a fiancée I've never met. I haven't even figured out my own bank account yet.

He turns the phone toward Roman. Roman looks at the photo exactly once and doesn't scroll down, like he doesn't need to. Nothing moves in his face. Only the hand on the table's edge has stopped, knuckles gone white.

es.hint: A fiancée out of thin air. More interesting than the fiancée: Roman's frozen hand.

opts.t: Pretty?

then.hint: "Pretty?" He's doing it on purpose. You know he's watching how you answer.

opts.t: Irrelevant.
Wrong fit for you.
then: Adrian stares for a beat, then laughs, a low rough sound straight from the chest.
I said she lands at six.

opts.t: Roman reaches over and switches Adrian's screen off. "I'll find out what she's here for."
then: Checking her out, or guarding against her?

opts.rthink: He's watching how I answer. I've known Sienna Reed seven years. If she's coming, it isn't to marry anyone.

opts.t: If I get married, are you running security for that too?
then: Two seconds of silence. Nothing in the cabin but the low drone of the engines.
Everyone who walks through your door is my problem. Her included.
opts.rthink: Mine. Standing behind him while he puts a ring on someone else—I didn't price that in three years ago.

opts.t: Adrian doesn't ask anything. He just watches Roman's frozen hand.
then: Roman draws the hand back and closes it slowly into a fist. The veins on the back of it stand up one by one.
Look at that hand. His mouth won't give me a thing, but those veins are confessing everything.
Adrian doesn't push. He files the hand away.
opts.rthink: Not because of her. Because once she walks in, what happened seven years ago starts leaking out of her mouth.

es: The captain's voice comes from up front: landing security needs his sign-off. Roman stands, pulls his jacket off the chair and shrugs it on, takes two steps, and turns back.
You say that like I'm six.

es.txt: I saw her photo a long time ago. Didn't mention it. Didn't want to watch you nod early.

es: Unsent. Three seconds later, a new one: Don't touch anything till we land. It came from his work number. So whose number is the phone on the table?
On the corner of the table, Roman's black encrypted phone lights up. A thumbnail flashes past: Adrian at seventeen, grinning like nothing could ever touch him.
He shouldn't look. The other half of his brain says: he watched you behind your back for three years. 'Fair' is suddenly a very handy word.
Adrian's hand moves before his brain signs off. His big palm comes down over the phone, fingertips still holding the keychain's warmth.

es.hint: He's up front; his low voice leaks through the door. The screen's unlocked. You have maybe a minute.

items: He still doesn't know, does he?
How long are you going to keep this up?
If he comes home, you failed.

apps.lockTxt: Passcode required. Hint: the date of the convenience-store night.
items: Adrian and Roman at seventeen and eighteen, on the curb outside the store. Adrian hasn't learned the sharp smile yet. Roman hasn't learned to hide anything.
Saved ten years ago. Opened once a year since, on the same date.
I should have told him before today.
Unsent · 3 years ago / 1 year ago / yesterday
Wed 08:05 · Pick up A. Go yourself.
Directions · a convenience store in Brooklyn · 41 times

win: He sets the phone back exactly where it was, same angle, even the window glare lined up on the glass.
He kept that photo. For ten years.
The draft is worse than the photo. It means he thought about coming back. He just didn't, again and again.
lose: Adrian looks once and turns the phone face down, palms gone damp. His heartbeat is louder than the snooping.
But the thumbnail of his seventeen-year-old face is already burned in.
skip: Adrian pushes the phone back without touching the glass. Some things he wants to hear out of Roman's own mouth.

es: The cabin door slides open and Roman comes back with a draft of cold air and a trace of cedar aftershave. The phone's at the same angle. The brightness isn't.
His grey eyes rest on the phone for half a second, then move to Adrian's face. He says nothing. That half second lasts as long as an interrogation.

es.hint: He's been through your phone. He put it back carefully, angle perfect. Carefully enough to look guilty.

opts.t: Roman holds his eyes for a second, swallows, and asks nothing.
Enjoy my phone?
then: Adrian doesn't blink. His chin lifts a fraction, a grin held down under the stubble.
You should really lock your screen.
Roman stares at him for two seconds, lets out a short breath through his nose, and drops it.

opts.t: Roman picks up the phone and sets a passcode right in front of him.
then: Four digits, punched in slow, like he wants them seen. Adrian knows them. The date of the convenience-store night.

es: Adrian opens his mouth, and the black phone lights up again. Unknown number. Voice message, 00:06. A red dot pulses in the corner.

es.title: Voice Message · Unknown Number
es.txt: A voice scraped raw by distortion, nothing human left in it: "Cross, walk away."

es: Something in Roman switches over. Spine straight, eyes gone flat. Not fear. A hound catching blood on the wind.
One swipe of his thumb and the message is dead. The veins stand out across the back of his hand, knuckles pinning the screen, so fast it almost cuts the air.
Fast enough that it's about Adrian not hearing. People hide things for two reasons: it could hurt them, or it could hurt you.
Cross — Roman's surname. Everyone he grew up with called him Roman. Only someone handling him like a codename would use the surname alone.
(Cross is Roman's surname. In his line of work, first names are for friends; surnames are for files and call signs.)

es.hint: He killed it. You didn't even catch whether the voice was a man's or a woman's.

opts.t: Play it again.
opts.rthink: Play it again and he'll ask who Cross is. Seven years are buried under that name. I haven't decided where to start digging.

opts.t: It called you Cross. It knows you.
then: A lot of people know me.
A lot of people tell you to stay away from me?
Roman doesn't answer. Static crackles in his earpiece; he presses two fingers to it like he's holding a wound shut.
opts.rthink: Fewer than five people alive call me Cross. One of them knows I'm on this plane today.

opts.t: Adrian reaches over and covers the hand holding the phone with his whole broad palm.
then: Roman's fingers lock. The back of his hand is burning under Adrian's palm, a vein jumping against it. He doesn't pull away.
I didn't ask if you were fine.
opts.rthink: His palm's hotter than my hand. I should pull away—pulling away is doing what the voice said. I don't.

t: roman
'Walk away.' Someone told me that seven years ago. Last time, I listened. I've spent seven years paying for it.

es: They start down; his ears pop and ache. New York rises out from under the clouds, grey-blue towers standing in the noon sun like a rack of upturned blades.
Roman stands, buttons his jacket, and presses the earpiece deeper. In that moment he isn't anybody's childhood friend. He's a wall that walks.
When the door opens, stay on my left.
Because there are forty-seven press credentials outside.
The door isn't open yet, but the sound gets there first: a muffled roar through the hull, like a whole stadium yelling on the other side of a wall.
The door opens and all of it pours in: shutters firing into one continuous rattle, dozens of throats shouting the same name. "Vale! Over here! Mr. Vale!"
Then the light. A black mass of bodies behind the barrier, long lenses lined up like rifle barrels; flashes going off in layers, white and scalding, turning the stair rail blue.
Closer in, microphones reach over the barrier to the foot of the stairs. Noon wind, heavy with jet fuel and hot asphalt, hits him full in the face.
At seven this morning he was smacking a jammed coffee maker in Brooklyn, in a building where nobody knew his last name. Now forty-seven cameras are waiting for him to come down a few steps.
Five years writing copy, begging people for one more look. Now all of New York is looking, and I'd like to find a crack in the door and crawl back through it.
Roman steps half a pace ahead and to the side, putting the whole wall of his shoulders in the way, and one big hand lands at the small of Adrian's back. Not resting. Holding.
Through two layers of cloth the heat of that hand brands straight in. Fingers spread, the heel of the palm pinned to his spine, steady as a driven nail.
Forty-seven cameras, and that's where he puts his hand. Is he here to protect me or to finish me off?

es.hint: Forty-seven cameras. Your hand is locked at the small of his back, his spine rigid under your palm. No security manual puts it there.

opts.t: (at his ear) Left side. Stay close.
Roman moves his hand from Adrian's back to his shoulder. Textbook escort position.
then: Through the wool, Adrian finds the hand almost too correct. Correct enough to leave a hollow behind.

opts.t: (right at his ear) Don't turn around. Turn around and your face is tomorrow's front page.
then: The hand at his back tightens, knuckles pressing through the fabric into the dip of his spine.

es: Warm breath grazes the back of his ear. Adrian's shoulders lock on instinct; the hair on his nape stands up.
The shutters come down like a cloudburst. Adrian turns his head and his nose nearly brushes Roman's jaw, close enough to smell cedar at his collar.
"Terrible timing," Adrian says through his teeth. The press is shouting: "ARE YOU ALEXANDER VALE'S SECRET SON?" "ARE YOU ENGAGED TO SIENNA REED?"
Engaged. He's known about that himself for less than an hour.

es.title: Step In as Adrian
es.hint: Forty-seven cameras, each question nastier than the last. That hand is still locked at your back. How do you stand here?

then: Adrian just smiles, chin up, pure Brooklyn don't-care. By tomorrow, that smile is on six front pages.
The hand at his back eases a fraction. Behind his shoulder, Roman's chest settles, like a breath let go.
He says it into the nearest mic, voice low and level as a nail going into wood, then adds —
One second of dead silence. Then the shutters double, hail on a tin roof.
Roman looks down at him, and something sits in those grey eyes, too deep to see the bottom of.
Who told you I was landing today?
The front-row reporter freezes, and his eyes flick, without permission, toward the back of the crowd.
Roman follows the look. His eyes go cold, and he turns his head to say something low into the earpiece.

then.title: Clue: Someone Tipped Them Off
then.txt: Only the family knew when he'd land, or about the engagement.

then: Adrian grabs Roman's wrist and hauls him level, tendons standing up across the back of his hand. Roman freezes half a second, then steps in at his side.
The flashes go off like a detonation, one solid sheet of white. This one will be on every phone by morning.
(very low) You did that on purpose.

es.cap: Wed 12:41 · On the stairs, his hand at your back
es.prompt: Private jet stairs on a bright tarmac, dozens of camera flashes, a tall broad-shouldered man in a black suit with an earpiece shielding a broad-shouldered stubbled dark-haired man in a tailored suit, almost his height, his hand firmly at the other man's lower back, both in their late twenties, press crowd blurred in the foreground, cinematic, no text
then: Roman glances at the photo. His throat works. He doesn't tell you to delete it.

es: The car door slams, shutting out the press and the heat together. Cold air hits his face; the leather seat is chilled stiff.
The phone in his pocket goes haywire. Dozens of notifications. Hundreds. His thigh goes numb from the buzzing.

es.txt: Vale heir spotted with mystery bodyguard.
cm: He is literally pulling him into his body.
That is not how a bodyguard looks at a client.

es: Blown up, the photo is worse than the moment. Roman's fingers are sunk into the fabric at his back, and in it Adrian is leaning toward him. He doesn't look like he wants to get away.
The internet has known them for eleven minutes and is already less subtle than either of them.
Forty-eight thousand likes. The guy leaning into him in that photo is me. I'll need an excuse. Wind, maybe.
Across from him, Roman's feed refreshes: a photo with no people in it, a hotel elevator from the security camera's angle, grey and hard. Caption: Too many cameras.
Adrian looks up. Roman is bent over his tablet, profile split into light and shadow by the window, earpiece wire against his neck, like he never posted a thing.

es.hint: You can comment under his post. Half of New York is watching. And he's sitting an arm's length across from you.

opts.t: Which camera got your good side?
then: Three seconds after it posts, a DM pops up. The man across from him hasn't even lifted his head.
Adrian doesn't. He drops the phone face down on his thigh and raises an eyebrow at Roman.
opts.rthink: Third row, east side, long lens—it caught him leaning into me. I've already had someone buy the original.

opts.t: Adrian likes the post and writes nothing.
then: The heart has barely turned red when the DM lands. Across the car, Roman's thumb is still on his screen.
opts.rthink: That red heart sits on my page where forty-eight thousand people can see it. I told him to undo it. I screenshotted it first.

opts.t: Adrian saves the press photo to a private album.
then: No post, no like. He just keeps it, his thumb resting a long time on the hand locked at his back.
Across from him, Roman is checking the route, one hard crease between his brows, with no idea.
opts.rthink: The park detour adds four minutes. Enough for someone to refocus twice. Stop thinking about that photo, Cross. Watch the route.

es: The private elevator runs from the garage straight to the top, not a single stop. While the numbers climb, Roman pulls a black tie from his inside pocket and knots it without a mirror — three moves, cinched up under his Adam's apple. There are Vale people upstairs waiting on the handover.
The Adrian in the mirror is six feet even, the new suit tight across his shoulders, collar yanked open a button, two days of stubble on his jaw. On his feet, the same old work boots, toes worn bald.
On his left wrist, the secondhand digital watch, its cracked strap still wound in black electrical tape. In this whole elevator, that and the boots are the only things he paid for himself.

es.title: THE TOP FLOOR
lines: The numbers top out and the car settles with the faintest dip. A sensor reads his phone; the panel lights: WELCOME HOME, ADRIAN VALE.
Ding. The doors part, and the far distance hits first: one unbroken wall of glass, Central Park flat as green felt, the Hudson a single line of white light.
Closer in, the light. The three o'clock sun slams through and turns sixty feet of oak floor into a river of gold that runs right up to the toes of his boots.
Only then the room itself: a double-height ceiling, a brass chandelier bigger than his bed, a bowl of white tuberoses heavy and sweet, a rug that swallows footsteps whole.
His leaky Brooklyn attic, coin laundry downstairs included, could be dropped in here whole and not fill one corner of this living room.
Adrian doesn't step off the entry mat. There's still Brooklyn grit on his soles; it leaves half a faint print on the white marble.
First thought: he wants it, badly enough to tighten his throat. Second thought, right behind it: this many windows, this many doors. Can one man cover them all?

es: Great. The marble under my boots probably costs more than a year of my rent. Watch your step.
Roman moves past him, hair cropped to the skull, a clear earpiece coil tucked behind his left ear. His grey eyes sweep the room once, measuring every window as a line of fire.
Yesterday I was worried about rent.
Today rent is worried about you.
Adrian laughs, low and rough. He follows Roman deeper in, room after room: a study, a wine cellar, a terrace you could land a helicopter on.
Outside the master bath there's a slick of water seeping from the shower, invisible on the black marble. Adrian's boot shoots out and all six feet of him pitch backward.
Roman catches him from behind — one big hand clamped on his hip, the other forearm barred across his chest, hard as a rail, hauling him back.
Two big men collide, chest to back. Through two layers of cloth Adrian can tell which heartbeat isn't his. Roman's collar smells of cedar.
Adrian doesn't move. He leans back instead, just a little, broad shoulders settling into Roman's chest — testing. Behind him, a breath catches hard.
Two seconds of silence. The fingers on his hip tighten once before they let go. Someone knocks on a doorframe down the hall; Roman steps back, jaw set like nothing happened.
That hand's bigger than it was ten years ago. Steadier, too. Hell. ...That lean back — put it down to the slip.

es.why: The catch at the bathroom door

es: The handover crew files out; the building manager leaves one note on the way: the master-bath shower valve is leaking, the plumber can't come till morning. Then it's quiet enough to hear the fridge hum.

Roman presses his earpiece back in, tugs his cuffs straight, and turns for another sweep. His back blocks half the hallway light; his shoes strike the oak one measured step at a time, like a countdown.

es.title: New Relationship Goal
es.txt: Get Roman to stay for one conversation he isn't paid for.

es.title: Relationship Goal
es.hint: The black card opens every door on this floor except his. Those black shoes are already at the threshold.

then: Can you stay a minute? Not for work.
Roman stops in the doorway. His broad shoulders check for a beat before he turns. Backlit by the hall, his grey eyes give nothing away.

then.hint: Not for work, he says. You've got ten work reasons to say no, and you don't reach for a single one.

opts.t: ...Let me clear the bedroom first.
Okay.
then: You asked if I could. You didn't ask how long.

opts.t: Roman lifts a hand and pulls the earpiece from his left ear; the clear coil drops against his white collar.

then: Mr. Vale's head of security says he has to clear the bedroom first.
He argues. His shoes stay nailed to the floor, not an inch of give, jaw locked tight.
If you leave, who checks the bed?
Roman's jaw shifts. Heat climbs slowly from his ears to the back of his cropped neck.
items.sub: See if his ears go red

then: I think the bedroom light's broken.

es: The master faces west. The last of the sun leaks through the sheers and cuts an orange gash across the charcoal linen.
Windows first. Under the bed last.
Under the bed's your department too?
Anywhere something can hide is my department.

Roman pulls the door shut behind them — only with it closed can you hear whether a window seal leaks. The latch bites with a click and the apartment cuts out. For the first time in ten years, it's just the two of them behind a closed door.

Roman drapes his jacket over a chair, tugs his tie loose, unhooks his cufflinks and rolls the white sleeves to the elbow. Veins stand along his forearms; the old scar shows across the inside of his wrist.

He works through it all: window locks, vents, the base of each lamp. His knuckles rap the glass, a dull solid sound. When he bends, the holster at the small of his back draws a hard line under his shirt.
Adrian sits on the edge of the bed, elbows on his knees, fingers laced, watching those big hands go over his room inch by inch.
Ten years, and he still finds the exits first. Same back then — and he used one the very next morning.

es.hint: The door's shut, the latch bitten home. Nobody's coming in. What you didn't finish at seventeen finally has a room big enough — and he's standing an arm's length away.

opts.t: Adrian stands and fists his loosened tie in one big hand.
then: The silk cinches tight across Adrian's knuckles and Roman has to bow his head. A palm's width between their faces; the vein in his neck is jumping hard enough to count.

then.hint: Your tie is wound in his fist, his knuckles against your throat, his breath on your stubble. One more inch down is all it would take.

opts.t: One more word right now and I'll regret it.
then: Roman's thumb settles on the inside of his wrist, right over the pulse, and stays a second before it lets go, slowly.

opts.t: Roman closes the inch and presses his mouth to Adrian's forehead — hard, brief. Only then does he let go of the tie.
then: The heat lingers on Adrian's forehead long after — harder to smooth out than the crease in that tie.

opts.t: Roman takes his hand, pries his fingers open one by one, and steps back.
then: A crease is left crushed into the black silk, like a cut that hasn't closed.

opts.rthink: He's got my tie in his fist; one inch down is all it takes. Rule one for three years: don't touch the principal. I'm saying it to myself twice.

opts.t: Adrian steps in until they're chest to chest, solid weight against solid weight. Not an accident.
then: Roman goes rigid for a beat. He doesn't back up. Through two shirts the heat of two chests meets, and his breathing drops low and heavy.
He's looking at Roman's mouth — pressed flat, a faint old split in the lower lip.
Roman's breath finally slips. His Adam's apple drags down hard. He doesn't touch Adrian. He doesn't move away either.
Don't ask me what I can't answer right now.
opts.rthink: I can't. I've lain on a rooftop six hours without moving, and right now I can't order myself half a step back.

opts.t: Adrian reaches into his loosened collar and runs a rough fingertip over the old scar under his collarbone.
then: He circles Adrian's wrist and lifts the hand off his chest. A hand that big, moving far too gently.
opts.rthink: That scar's from the missing seven years. An inch lower there's another. For that one I haven't even worked out a lie.

opts.t: Adrian hooks a hand around the back of his neck and kisses him.
then: One second, Roman doesn't move, strung tight as a drawn bow. The next, his palm locks onto Adrian's waist and there's no space left.
He kisses back once. Just once. Short and hard, stubble scraping stubble. Then he wrenches himself still, forehead to Adrian's.
You don't know what you're doing.
Finishing something from ten years ago. I know exactly.
Roman opens his eyes, the grey gone dark as slate. They drop to Adrian's mouth and stay.
Ten years ago I stopped. I have to stop now too.
opts.rthink: Ten years ago I stopped so I wouldn't ruin him. Now I stop because I wouldn't stop. He tastes like mint—the kind I quit.

opts.t: When you're done — don't go.
then: Roman's hand stops on the window lock. The lamp catches the stubble along his jaw. This time he doesn't say no right away.
Ms. Reed is due at six. I'm the one who clears the elevator.
Roman checks the steel watch on his wrist, pulls out the chair with his jacket on it, and sits.
Twenty minutes. The rest belongs to the job.
opts.rthink: Twenty minutes, calculated. Three for the elevator. That leaves seventeen, and I'm not wasting one more second on window locks.

es.title: After the Bedroom Door Closed
es.teaser: It's full dark. The bedside lamp is the only light. He hasn't left, and his tie is half undone.
then: Outside the sky sinks to ink and Manhattan lights up floor by floor. The bedside lamp is the only light in the room, amber, stretching their shadows long.
Roman hasn't left. He stands at the edge of the bed where Adrian sits, knee against knee, wool rasping over wool.
Roman lifts a hand and drags the rough backs of his knuckles, slow, behind Adrian's ear. The same spot his thumb found ten years ago.
Here. That night, it was here.
I remember more than you think.
He leans down, one hand braced on the mattress beside Adrian; it sinks under his weight. His forehead comes to rest against Adrian's.
Their breathing knots together, warm, with a cool edge of mint. Neither of them closes the last half inch.
Adrian doesn't say stop. He fists the front of Roman's shirt, cotton crushing in his grip, and hauls him down an inch.
Roman's mouth grazes the corner of his and stops. Eyes shut, brow knotted, the veins standing out on the hand braced by Adrian's hip — fighting himself.
His hand is shaking. Roman Cross, who can strip a gun blind, and his hand is shaking.
His earpiece spits static: "Sector B clear."
A long moment later Roman straightens, and presses his thumb hard to Adrian's lower lip, like a seal.

es: Roman steps back first. Not running — handing the choice back. He fixes his tie, thick knuckles smoothing the silk twice, slower than usual.
If this keeps happening, we need rules.

es.title: Boundary
es.hint: Roman hands the choice back to you. Whatever rules you set, this man will follow to the letter, like orders.

then: Roman doesn't answer. He tries to flatten the corner of his mouth and fails.
Roman nods, brow creased, like he's committing a security protocol to memory.
Then may I fix your collar?
You're sure you want that in writing?

es: 5:40. Roman goes to look at the leaking valve in the master bath. Thirty seconds later there's a dull bang, the roar of water hitting tile, and one low, bitten-off curse.
Adrian gets there fast. The cartridge has blown, water shooting sideways, and Roman is down on one knee in it, one big hand clamped over the outlet, soaked head to foot.
Quit wrestling it. Shutoff's under the sink.
He yanks the cabinet open, kneels in the wet, finds the brass valve and cranks it all the way. The water dies. His Brooklyn landlord never once picked up the phone; he could do this blind.
The words land on the wet tile and neither of them picks them up. Roman goes to rinse off in the guest bath and change out of his go-bag. When the door opens again, a cloud of steam rolls out first.
Roman's hair is wet, cropped short and standing on end, beaded with water. The black T-shirt is still damp, clinging to his shoulders and chest, mapping every hard line of muscle.
Grey sweatpants, bare feet on the oak, a towel slung around his neck. A drop of water slides down the side of his throat, over his Adam's apple, and under the collar.
So I looked. He's the one who blew the valve. How wet he got isn't my problem.

es.hint: He caught you looking. The damp shirt is plastered to him, water still running. Technically, that's not in the rules.

opts.t: Looking wasn't on the list.
then: Roman looks up through wet hair and holds his eyes for two full seconds.
opts.rthink: There's a dress shirt in the go-bag. I reached for the T-shirt first. He thinks I didn't have a choice.

opts.t: Adrian walks over, pulls the towel off his neck, and dries his hair for him.
then: Roman goes still, lowers his head, and lets him. Under the towel his cropped hair bristles against Adrian's palms, steam rising off him.
opts.rthink: Under the towel he can't see my face. Good. No client should see what it's doing right now.

es.title: Lobby Call
es.txt: Concierge: Ms. Reed has arrived — 6:00 PM on your calendar. Release the private elevator?

es: Roman grabs his phone and pulls up the elevator camera. On screen a woman stands alone in the walnut car; she glances up and nods at the lens, like she knows exactly who's watching.
He's into a spare white shirt in three moves, buttoned to the throat, wet hair raked back — fast as a man scrubbing a scene.
Ding. The doors slide open and Sienna steps out: chin-length dark-honey hair, pale green eyes, an ivory silk blouse under a sharply cut camel coat.
A slim chain at her throat carries a signet ring. Low heels, almost silent on the floor, an oxblood leather briefcase in one hand, the faintest trace of fig.

Like she's come straight from a board meeting and this was on her way. Her first look is for Adrian, boots to stubble, like she's checking a due-diligence file. Her second lands on Roman — and stays too long to be a first.
She steps in and straightens Adrian's open collar, fingertips resting near his collarbone a second too long. The ring on her chain swings down, cold metal against his skin.
Roman doesn't come closer. Doesn't interrupt. The hand at his side slowly closes into a fist, veins rising one by one across the back of it, knuckles going white.
Fine. I'm the prop. She's fixing my collar and measuring his fist.
Sienna's smile widens — and the wider it gets, the less she means it. She isn't touching Adrian. She's using him as a probe, and testing Roman.

t: sienna
Same as ever. The more he cares, the stiller he gets. Seven years and nothing's changed.
roman
Get your hand off him. ...I don't have the right to say that.

es: She sits, crosses her legs, snaps open the brass clasps of the briefcase, and slides an engagement agreement across to Adrian: a law firm's gilt letterhead, a red wax seal, twenty pages of asset clauses.
Adrian turns to the last page. In the signature block, the ink is long dry: ADRIAN VALE.
Someone sent me in with this to play the dutiful fiancée. But I read the last page.
Roman takes the document. At the signature his pupils snap tight and his fingers whiten on the edge of the paper — then he's back to normal.
He knows that handwriting. Roman's looking at that signature like he's identifying a body.

es.title: Roman Recognized Something
es.txt: Whoever forged it knows how Adrian used to sign his name.

es: The phone in his pocket won't stop buzzing: YOU WERE ADDED TO: VALE FAMILY. The member count climbs. 12. 18. 27.
(glancing at his screen) That's Evelyn. She wants to see what your first words are.
The more you say that, the more I want to.

es.hint: Nobody's welcoming a relative. They're assessing a new variable.
es.name: VALE FAMILY

then: Adrian sends nothing, thumb resting on the edge of the screen. The read count ticks up and up. Twenty-seven people. Nobody types.
(with a glance at Roman) Listened to your bodyguard. Silence is a statement. Not bad.
Three seconds later, Evelyn replies with a period. Cold as a nail.
(trying not to laugh) Welcome to the Vales.
One full minute of silence. The typing bubble next to Julian's avatar flickers twice and dies.
Roman watches the screen and his eyes go cold by degrees, a muscle ticking under the skin of his jaw.

items.t: Drop the agreement photo in the group
then: Adrian shoots the signature page and drops it in the group with a whoosh. No caption.

then.title: The Group Goes Silent
then.txt: Twenty-seven members. Not one dares reply.

then: Roman says nothing. The way he looks at Adrian has changed, like he's seeing him clearly for the first time.

skip: Adrian mutes the group and sets the phone face down on the marble with a clack.

es: At night the penthouse is something else. Every light is off but a cold white strip along the baseboards. Beyond the glass the city spreads out like coals that won't burn down.

Sienna didn't leave till nine. She'd ordered dinner in herself — "Vale chefs report the menu to Evelyn." Roman insisted on walking her down to the garage himself. Before the doors closed, she held them with one hand and lowered her voice.
Ask him where he went for seven years.
The trace of fig hangs in the entry long after she's gone. Adrian leans in the bedroom doorway, thumb working over the taped strap of the cheap watch on his left wrist.

es.hint: He's still down in the garage. Three rings — then he hung up himself.

Roman changes all at once. His spine goes straight, his right hand drifts silently to the small of his back, and the muscles of his jaw stand out in ridges.

es.title: YOU SHOULDN'T HAVE COME HOME
es.txt: THE VALE NAME DOESN'T BELONG TO YOU.

es: The first two are the penthouse windows. The third resolves block by block: Roman outside the elevator, white shirt, hard profile — tonight's shirt. Shot from somewhere high where nobody should be.
A red laser dot sits steady on the left side of his chest, right over the heart. Beneath it: COME ALONE TOMORROW. OR YOUR BODYGUARD DIES FIRST.
East rooftop. They've had a lens on him for half an hour at least and never pulled the trigger — it's me they want, not him. Fine. Come and get it.

es.txt: Last time someone told me to stay away from you, I listened. Not this time.

es: Unsent. Three seconds later, a new one. Two words: You okay?
All day he's been demanding to know where Roman went for ten years. Now there's only one thing he needs to be sure of: that red dot doesn't land on that white shirt again tomorrow.

en: The door opens. Roman slips in sideways, locks it behind him, and the first thing he does is seize Adrian's arm and yank him away from the window.
He rips the curtains shut. The room drops into dark, nothing but the lamp's amber circle catching a sheen of sweat at his temple.
His hand stays clamped on Adrian's upper arm, fingers sunk into solid muscle. He looks down at him, chest heaving.
You sent it to me first.
Most people think of themselves first.
He sets his phone on the table and pushes it across. On screen: the full security plan for tomorrow's welcome gala, every entrance marked in red.
From now on, you see everything. All of it.
Cards on the table. If he'd done this ten years ago, think how much trouble we'd have saved.

zh: Adrian盯着那条“你还好吗”，拇指悬在屏幕上停了好几秒，只回：没事。你换班吧。
Adrian低头。他的右手不知什么时候已经扣在左手腕上，拇指死死压着那圈黑胶布。

zh.hint: 他知道你在撒谎。你还想把他推远一点——推出那粒红点够得着的地方。

opts.t: 晚安，Roman。
then: Roman没回晚安。只发来一句：我过来。
Adrian攥着手机，手背的青筋一根根绷了起来。
opts.rthink: 晚安，就是让我滚。他收到的东西跟我有关——不然他不会这么客气。

opts.t: Adrian关掉手机，屏幕朝下扣在床上。
then: 一分钟后，门外传来脚步声，沉，稳，停在他的门口。
opts.rthink: 已读不回，接着关机。三年来他第一次让我找不到。手已经搭上枪套，人往他门口走了。

zh: 敲门声。三下，很轻，指节落在实木门板上，闷闷的。
Adrian背靠着门滑坐下去，没开。宽阔的后背贴着冰凉的木头，照片里那粒红点还烙在眼前。
你一紧张就摸左手腕。我不用看都知道。
他的手，确实正攥在左手腕上，攥得那圈胶布硌进皮肉。
我不走。今晚就坐在这儿。
门板另一侧传来布料擦过木头的沙沙声，和一声压低的闷哼——他真的坐下了，隔着一扇门，背对着背。
Adrian把后脑抵在门上。隔着两寸厚的实木，他听得见那个人的呼吸，又沉又稳。

t: roman
他在保护我。他以为我看不出来。

zh.title: 路线：隐瞒
zh.txt: 等Roman发现威胁，信任会重创——也会第一次知道，你想保护他。

en: Adrian stares at You okay?, thumb hovering over the glass for long seconds. Then he types: Fine. Go off shift.
Adrian looks down. At some point his right hand closed around his left wrist; his thumb is pressing hard on the black tape.

en.hint: He knows you're lying. You still want to push him further away — out of that red dot's reach.

opts.t: Goodnight, Roman.
then: Roman doesn't say goodnight. He sends: Coming over.
Adrian's grip tightens on the phone, the veins standing out across the back of his hand.
opts.rthink: 'Goodnight' means get lost. Whatever he got, it's about me. Otherwise he wouldn't be this polite.

opts.t: Adrian kills the phone and drops it face down on the bed.
then: A minute later, footsteps outside — heavy, steady — stopping at his door.
opts.rthink: Read, no reply, then dark. First time in three years I can't reach him. My hand's on the holster and I'm already walking to his door.

en: A knock. Three times, very soft, knuckles on solid wood.
Adrian slides down with his back to the door and doesn't open it. Broad shoulders against cold wood, the red dot still burned into his eyes.
You touch your left wrist when you're scared. I don't need to see it to know.
His hand is on his left wrist, gripping so hard the taped strap bites skin.
I'm not leaving. I'll sit right here tonight.
On the other side, fabric rasps down the wood with a low grunt. He really sat down. Back to back, a door between them.
Adrian rests the back of his head on the door. Through two inches of oak he can hear the man breathing, slow and even.

t: roman
He's protecting me. He thinks I can't tell.

en.title: Route: The Secret He Kept
en.txt: When Roman finds the threat, trust will crack. And he'll learn you were trying to protect him.

zh: Adrian第一次真正用上这部加密手机。哑光黑机身，沉得压手。屏幕亮起：VALE安保，最高权限。是否追踪私人号码？

zh.hint: 按下去，内部安保会留下记录。你的指纹，会出现在某个人的日志里。

opts.t: 确认追踪。
then: 地图飞快缩放，城市的街道像碎玻璃一样拼合：不是城外，不是黑市服务器，是VALE大厦内部中继。
opts.rthink: 日志里跳出他的名字。我第一件事不是查他，是查还有谁看得见这条记录。这栋楼里，有人看得见。

opts.t: 先存好截图，再确认追踪。
then: 截图存进三个地方，他才按下确认。地图最后停在：VALE大厦内部中继。
opts.rthink: 截图存了三处才动手，比我想的冷静。这股冷静像他父亲——这话我这辈子不会当面说。

zh: Adrian脸上的表情一点点褪干净，只剩下颌线绷成一道冷硬的棱。威胁不是从Vale家外面来的。
手机立刻在掌心里炸响。
为什么内部安保刚刚标记了你的账户？
“因为这栋楼里有人想让你死。”他的嗓音平得吓人。
电话那头安静了一秒。Adrian听见一声极轻的金属响——是枪套搭扣被拨开的声音。
我去查中继。你哪儿都别去。
“你一个人去？”Adrian已经站了起来，一把抓过椅背上的西装外套。
这次不是一个人。你在电话这头，一直别挂。
他要是敢在电话那头断线，我就亲自下楼，把那个中继拆成零件。

t: roman
内部中继。能动它的人，一只手数得过来。其中一个，今天刚给我发过语音。

zh.title: 重大线索：威胁来自Vale内部

en: For the first time Adrian really uses the encrypted phone — matte black, heavy in the palm. The screen lights: VALE SECURITY / EXECUTIVE OVERRIDE. Trace private sender?

en.hint: Press it and internal security will log it. Your fingerprint lands in somebody's records.

opts.t: Confirm the trace.
then: The map zooms fast, streets snapping together like broken glass. Not out of state. Not a black-market server. VALE TOWER INTERNAL RELAY.
opts.rthink: His name pops up in the internal log. My first move isn't checking on him—it's checking who else can see it. Someone in this building can.

opts.t: Save the screenshots first, then trace.
then: He saves the screenshots in three places before he confirms. The map stops on: VALE TOWER INTERNAL RELAY.
opts.rthink: Three backups before he pulled the trigger. Cooler than I expected. That's his father in him, and I'll never say so to his face.

en: The expression drains off Adrian's face until only the hard ridge of his jaw is left. The threat didn't come from outside the family.
The phone goes off in his palm immediately.
Why did Internal Security just flag your account?
"Because someone inside this building wants you dead." His voice is frighteningly flat.
One second of silence on the line. Then a faint metallic click — a holster strap coming loose.
I'm going to the relay. Don't go anywhere.
"Alone?" Adrian is already on his feet, grabbing his suit jacket off the chair.
Not this time. You stay on the line. Don't hang up.
If he so much as drops this call, I'm going down there and taking that relay apart with my bare hands.

t: roman
The internal relay. I can count the people with access on one hand. One of them sent me a voice message today.

en.title: Major Clue: It Came From Inside Vale

zh: Adrian盯着那张准星压在Roman胸口的照片，下颌咬得发酸，一个字一个字打：有种试试。
发送。三秒，对方已读。然后，一张新照片慢慢传了过来。
不是Roman。是一张旧照：十七岁的他和十八岁的Roman并肩坐在便利店门口的台阶上，一人一罐冰可乐，霓虹把两张脸照得发红。
照片背面第一次露出一行字，黑色马克笔，用力得划破了相纸：他本来就不该回来找你。
Adrian的呼吸停了一拍。窗外，雨点开始一颗颗砸上玻璃。

zh.hint: 对方知道十年前那晚。知道那晚的人，本该只有你们两个。

opts.t: Adrian把照片转发给Roman。
opts.rthink: 这张照片我只存过一份。能拿到它的人，一定在我睡着的时候，离我不到一臂。

opts.t: 回复：你是谁？
then: 对方没再回。已读，然后头像变成了一片死灰。
opts.rthink: 十秒没回。我在数从这儿到他门口几步：十一步。第十二步之前，他最好开口。

zh: 门外走廊里，电梯“叮”了一声。皮鞋声，一步，又一步——Adrian分不清是谁。
屏幕黑了。房间里只剩雨声，和他自己的心跳。

t: roman
那张照片只有一份。我以为它在我手机里。

zh.title: 路线：敌人激进
zh.txt: 危险升级最快，也最早拿到十年前的线索。

en: Adrian stares at the red dot on Roman's chest, jaw clenched until it aches, and types two words, letter by letter: Try me.
Sent. Three seconds. Read. Then a new photo begins to load.
Not Roman. An old photo: him at seventeen and Roman at eighteen, shoulder to shoulder on the convenience-store step, a cold can each, the neon burning their faces red.
On the back, words he's never seen before, black marker pressed so hard it tore the paper: HE WAS NEVER SUPPOSED TO COME BACK FOR YOU.
Adrian's breath stops. Outside, rain starts hitting the glass, drop by heavy drop.

en.hint: Whoever this is knows about that night. Only the two of you were supposed to.

opts.t: Adrian forwards the photo to Roman.
opts.rthink: I only ever kept one copy of that photo. Whoever has it got within arm's reach of me while I slept.

opts.t: Reply: Who are you?
then: No reply. Read. Then the profile picture goes dead grey.
opts.rthink: Ten seconds, no answer. I'm counting steps to his door: eleven. He'd better say something before I take the twelfth.

en: Out in the hall, the elevator dings. Hard soles, one step, then another. Adrian can't tell whose.
The screen goes black. Nothing left in the room but the rain and his own heartbeat.

t: roman
There's only one copy of that photo. I thought it was on my phone.

en.title: Route: The Enemy Escalates
en.txt: Danger escalates fastest, and the clue from ten years ago comes early.

ja: Adrian stares at the red dot on Roman's chest, jaw clenched until it aches, and types two words, letter by letter: Try me.
Sent. Three seconds. Read. Then a new photo begins to load.
Not Roman. An old photo: him at seventeen and Roman at eighteen, shoulder to shoulder on the convenience-store step, a cold can each, the neon burning their faces red.
On the back, words he's never seen before, black marker pressed so hard it tore the paper: HE WAS NEVER SUPPOSED TO COME BACK FOR YOU.
Adrian's breath stops. Outside, rain starts hitting the glass, drop by heavy drop.

ja.hint: Whoever this is knows about that night. Only the two of you were supposed to.

opts.t: Adrian forwards the photo to Roman.
opts.rthink: I only ever kept one copy of that photo. Whoever has it got within arm's reach of me while I slept.

opts.t: Reply: Who are you?
then: No reply. Read. Then the profile picture goes dead grey.
opts.rthink: Ten seconds, no answer. I'm counting steps to his door: eleven. He'd better say something before I take the twelfth.

ja: Out in the hall, the elevator dings. Hard soles, one step, then another. Adrian can't tell whose.
The screen goes black. Nothing left in the room but the rain and his own heartbeat.

t: roman
There's only one copy of that photo. I thought it was on my phone.
